All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.

### Unreleased[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#unreleased)

### 0.4.0 (2026-11-07)[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#0-4-0-2026-11-07)

#### Added[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#added)

- ADVISOR module (`Waynestate\Helmet\Advisor\HelmetModule`): a coding agent that runs ADVISOR gains two read-only tools. `helmet_headers` returns the headers and CSP HELMET sends, built by `SecurityHeaders::build()`, each header and directive with its reason, plus how the app folder is wired to HELMET and the settings that change the answer. `helmet_php_support` reads the PHP constraint from the app's `composer.json` and reports the support status of its floor, and of every version it allows, from the CREED policy ADVISOR bundles, read with HELMET's own `JsonFilePolicySource` and `VersionStatus`. Both take one path inside the project, run in-process, write nothing and never read `.env`. `waynestate/advisor` is a dev dependency and a suggestion, never a requirement. New docs guide: "Your coding agent (ADVISOR)".
- `Headers\HeaderReasons`: one reason per header and CSP directive, next to the policy; a test fails when one is added without a reason.
- The Proof page records its last run.
- Logging: every web request record carries `extra.http` (method, path without the query string, client address as PHP saw it). Long token-like path segments are masked.
- Metrics: opt-in request metrics. `HELMET_METRICS_STORAGE` (`apcu`, `redis` or `sqlite`, each one of promphp's own adapters) turns on `helmet_http_request_duration_seconds`, a histogram by route group, method and status class whose `_count` is the request count, and `helmet_csp_violations_total` by directive (Laravel's CSP report endpoint counts each report it logs). Every label is bounded by HELMET, never by the client: unknown routes, methods and directives fold into `other`. Laravel gains the `RecordRequestMetrics` global middleware, added only when metrics are enabled with a store; raw PHP gains `helmet_metrics_track()` and `helmet_metrics_env()`. Off by default: an app that sets nothing behaves exactly as before.
- Metrics: `helmet_php_eol_timestamp_seconds` (the end of security support for the running PHP, from CREED's policy; days left is `(helmet_php_eol_timestamp_seconds - time()) / 86400`), `wsu_stack_info{package,version}` for every installed `waynestate/*` package (ADR-0011), and `helmet_metrics_storage_up`, so a store outage shows on the dashboard while the info metrics keep answering. Laravel's `/metrics` reads `helmet.policy_path` when no `PolicySource` is bound.
- Docs: the Metrics guide covers what each metric means, how labels stay bounded, picking a store, turning metrics on for one site (Laravel and raw PHP), the scrape config and PromQL; troubleshooting covers a 403 on Apache, empty request panels and an `unknown` support status.
- Grafana dashboard (`docs/grafana/helmet.json`): `job` and `instance` variables on every query, and new panels for targets down, days to PHP end of support, stack packages, requests by route group and by status class, latency p50 and p95, p95 by route group, server errors, metrics storage and CSP violations by directive. Checked by importing it into Grafana 12 through the API against a local Prometheus scraping three HELMET apps, one per store. Scrape health is a state timeline (up or down per target) and the version panels are bar charts.

#### Fixed[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#fixed)

- Metrics: `helmet_php_version_status` looked up the full PHP release (`8.3.12`) in CREED's policy, which names versions by major.minor (`8.3`), so every real app reported `unknown`. It now looks up major.minor.
- Policy: `JsonFilePolicySource` read each component as a flat version map, but CREED's `policy.json` (and its schema) keeps the versions under `versions`, so against the real file the ribbon never warned and the PHP support metrics said `unknown`. It now reads both shapes, skips a version with no `security_until`, and treats one with no `active_until` as security-only.
- Metrics: `helmet_info`'s `helmet_version` is the tagged version (`0.3.1`), the same form `wsu_stack_info` uses, not Composer's normalized `0.3.1.0`.
- Metrics: `helmet_metrics()` read the scraper's token only from `$_SERVER['HTTP_AUTHORIZATION']`, which Apache with mod_php (Citadel's images) never sets, so a correct token got 403 there. It now also reads `REDIRECT_HTTP_AUTHORIZATION` and `getallheaders()` (`BearerToken::fromServer()`). Found by scraping HELMET's own front page in a php:8.5 Apache container.
- Grafana dashboard: the data source was declared under `inputs`, which Grafana's import ignores, so every panel pointed at an unresolved `${DS_PROMETHEUS}`; it is now `__inputs` (with `__requires`). "Scrape health" joined `up` to `helmet_info`, which drops exactly the targets that are down; it now graphs `up` directly.

#### Changed[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#changed)

- The canonical repository is git.wayne.edu (ADR-0021); docs, links and package metadata no longer point at the archived nougat copy.

#### Security[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#security)

- The front-page deploy layer moves to Symfony 7.4.23 (symfony/http-foundation and symfony/yaml advisories, including CVE-2026-118514).

### 0.3.1 (2026-11-05)[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#0-3-1-2026-11-05)

No breaks: new boot warning for a broad trusted-proxy list, `helmet_csp_nonce_swap()`, `GenericErrorResponse::clientError()`, a Grafana dashboard, a contract test suite and the docs site, plus docs and deploy-layer refreshes.

- Docs: the docs theme sits closer to the front page and the brand board. Page titles carry the hero's play call in the coach's marker ("The playbook") and the board's wordmark rule (one thin line with a short gold bar, laid in after the title is chalked in) in place of the thick green rule, and the phone Menu is one of the hero's dashed call chips (solid gold on hover or open) instead of a solid green bar. Light and dark; motion only with `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`.
- Docs: BEST_PRACTICES H45 is `Documented`. `tests/Support/ConfigDocsTest.php` fails when a `helmet_boot()` option or a `config/helmet.php` key is missing from the README or the configuration reference, and both now list every option and key.
- Docs: BEST_PRACTICES H14 is `Partly enforced` with tests on every path (raw PHP over HTTP, PSR-15 error-middleware order, Laravel aborted and unmatched requests); the README and the PSR-15 guide say to mount HELMET outermost, after the error middleware in a Slim-style app.
- Added: `tests/Contract/HeaderContractTest.php`, a contract suite that runs the same request and config through raw PHP (`helmet_boot()` in a `php -S` child), the PSR-15 middleware, the Laravel `web` group and a Laravel JSON answer, and asserts the contract headers agree byte for byte apart from the nonce; README section "One contract, every path", BEST_PRACTICES H10 names the suite.
- Docs: the docs pages wear the front page. Every page under `site/docs/` carries the front page's slate header and main menu (Docs underlined in gold), Graduate titles, numbered gold binder tabs on each section (the "On this page" list carries the same numbers), the coach's marker on the sidebar groups with a berry "you are here" ring around the current page, code on the scoreboard's black glass with a gold Copy tab and the scoreboard's tabs over code tabs, callouts as stamped play cards, the depth chart's green bars on tables, previous and next as laminated play cards, and the end zone as the footer. Dark mode is the hero's chalkboard. The theme lives in `docs/theme/helmet.css` and `docs/_header.html`, named by the `theme` key in `docs/docs.json`; the shared builder and kit are resynced from SQUIRE `0778fed` (theme hook, callouts, code tabs, task lists, a copy button that reports a working copy, keyboard-reachable scrolling code) and not edited here. Motion only with `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`.
- Added: `helmet.broad_trusted_proxy` (warning, logged once at boot when the resolved trusted-proxy list holds a broad entry, an IPv4 range shorter than `/16` or an IPv6 range shorter than `/48`, with `event` and `entries` in the context), so a whole-network trust is hard to miss in the logs; `TrustedProxies::broadEntries()` does the detection, both the Laravel provider and the raw PHP `helmet_boot()` emit it through the configured logger, and a failing logger never breaks the boot. Opt out with `helmet.warn_broad_proxies` (env `HELMET_WARN_BROAD_PROXIES`, default true) or `warn_broad_proxies: false` in `helmet_boot()`. Tests: `tests/Proxy/BroadEntriesTest.php`, `tests/Laravel/BroadProxyWarningTest.php`, `tests/FunctionsBroadProxyTest.php`; BEST_PRACTICES H21 is now `Partly enforced`.
- Docs: README and the raw PHP guide gain "Readiness is a separate check": `/up` stays liveness-only, dependency checks go on a separate `/ready` path with a short timeout and a fixed 503 body, and Laravel apps keep them out of the `DiagnosingHealth` listener; BEST_PRACTICES H34 is `Documented`.
- Added: a Grafana dashboard for the HELMET metrics (`docs/grafana/helmet.json`, uid `helmet-fleet`) with panels for apps reporting, HELMET and PHP versions in use, PHP support status, apps by instance, and scrape health; it imports into any Grafana through a `DS_PROMETHEUS` datasource input, and `tests/Support/GrafanaDashboardTest.php` pins its shape. The metrics guide gains a "Graph it in Grafana" section with a sample `scrape_configs` stanza. `docs/` was never export-ignored, so the dashboard already ships in the dist archive.
- Added: `helmet_csp_nonce_swap(string $html, string $nonce, string $placeholder = 'CSP_NONCE_SLOT_FOR_HELMET')` for raw PHP apps serving a built Vue/Vite page: it replaces every occurrence of the build-time placeholder (the value Vite's `html.cspNonce` stood in for) with the response nonce from `helmet_boot()`, HTML-escaped exactly like `helmet_csp_nonce_meta()` escapes it. A placeholder shorter than 16 characters throws `InvalidArgumentException`, as does an empty nonce, and a page without the placeholder is returned unchanged. Pure function: no output, no headers, no globals. Covered by `tests/FunctionsNonceSwapTest.php`.
- Added: the docs site. `bin/docs-site.php` (Squire's shared builder) turns `docs/` into `site/docs/`: the Overview page carries the README opening and a generated table of every `HELMET_` environment variable the package reads. `composer docs` rebuilds it, `composer ci` checks it through `composer docs:check`, and the front page links it.
- Docs: BEST_PRACTICES H53 is `Documented` (SESAME owns the logout headers, `Clear-Site-Data` without `"cookies"`) and H41 is `Partly enforced` (three events are logged, authentication failures belong to SESAME).
- Docs: README section "Debug output stays off in production" names the two settings that decide whether a visitor sees a trace (PHP `display_errors`, Laravel `APP_DEBUG`), points at Squire's deploy `php.ini`, and documents the `helmet.warn_debug` opt-out; BEST_PRACTICES H43 is now `Documented`.
- Changed: the front-page deploy layer pins HELMET ^0.3, PROCTOR ^0.4 and CREED ^0.1 (lock: HELMET 0.3.0, PROCTOR 0.4.0, CREED 0.1.6).
- Changed: CI pins Preflight 0.1.4 (GitLab component includes and the GitHub reusable workflow at its tag commit); the deploy layer sets minimum-stability to stable.
- Docs: the sample metrics output shows 0.3.0.
- Added: `GenericErrorResponse::clientError(int $status)` returns a fixed 4xx page (status, headers, body) for client faults, with its own title and sentence for 400, 401, 403, 404, 405, 410 and 429 and the Bad request text for any other 4xx; a status outside the 400s throws `InvalidArgumentException`, and nothing from the request or an exception reaches the body. An app calls it from its router; nothing wires it into `helmet_boot()` automatically.
- Added: an accessibility gate for the site (axe-core in Playwright, Docker). `scripts/a11y.sh` and `scripts/a11y.ps1` check `site/index.html` and every page under `site/docs/` in light and dark at 360 px and 1280 px, and fail on any WCAG 2.2 AA violation; `tools/a11y/check.mjs` is the runner.
- Fixed: two violations the new gate found. A code block wider than its box now joins the tab order so a keyboard user can scroll it (axe `scrollable-region-focusable`, WCAG 2.1.1), and table-of-contents sub-items get a full-width link target of at least 24 px (axe `target-size`, WCAG 2.5.8). Both come from syncing the Squire-owned docs kit (`bin/docs-site.php`, `site/assets/docs.css`, `site/assets/docs.js`) to the current stack version, and the docs site and agent-ready files are rebuilt from it.
- Changed: the docs site renders fenced blocks tagged `tab=` as a labeled tablist (the previous builder ignored the tag and stacked the blocks), and the changelog mirror keeps its top-level heading, per the current shared builder.

### 0.3.0 (2026-11-03)[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#0-3-0-2026-11-03)

- This is a pre-1.0 minor: apps that pin `^0.2` stay on 0.2.x until they move their constraint to `^0.3`. The proxy and forwarded-header changes below make some requests resolve differently (an empty `HELMET_PROXIES=` now trusts nobody), so read the Security lines first.
- Docs: BEST_PRACTICES H14, H13 and H41 say what is tested and what is not (error page headers on the raw PHP path, WayneUI assets, session hardening events).
- Added: opt-in generic error page for raw PHP. `helmet_boot(['error_handler' => ['enabled' => true]])` installs an exception handler that logs the full detail at `error` level and shows a fixed 500 page with no exception text; `Waynestate\Helmet\Error\GenericErrorResponse::build()` returns the same response as data. Off by default; Laravel keeps its own handler.
- Added: two structured security events, `helmet.request_refused` (warning, logged when the request-forgery guard answers 403, with `event`, `method`, `path`, `sec_fetch_site` and `origin_present` in the context) and `helmet.forwarded_for_rejected` (warning, logged by `ClientIp::resolve()` when it fails closed on an unparseable `X-Forwarded-For` entry, with `event`, `reason` and `peer` in the context); the Origin value, cookies, Authorization, the header and the bad entry are never logged, and a failing logger never changes the 403 or the resolved IP.
- Added: `helmet.debug_enabled_in_production` (warning, logged once by the Laravel adapter at boot when the app boots with `app.debug` true in the production environment, with `event` in the context); opt out with `helmet.warn_debug` (env `HELMET_WARN_DEBUG`, default true), and a failing logger never breaks the boot.
- Security: `ClientIp` fails closed on an unparseable `X-Forwarded-For` entry (for example `203.0.113.5:443`): it returns the peer instead of walking on to an earlier, client-chosen entry, so a malformed header can no longer steer the resolved client IP.
- Security: IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses (`::ffff:a.b.c.d`) are unmapped before matching trusted proxies, for both the peer and the forwarded entries, so a dual-stack proxy still matches its IPv4 entry instead of slipping past the trust check.
- Security: `X-Forwarded-Proto` now follows one rule everywhere, the last non-empty value in `HttpsDetector` and the Laravel normalizer, and the normalizer decides trust with the list Laravel itself uses (`trustedproxy.proxies` when set, else `helmet.proxies`, with `*` and `**` trusting every peer as in Symfony), so HELMET and the framework can no longer disagree about which value to read or from whom to accept it.
- Security: an explicitly empty `HELMET_PROXIES=` now trusts nobody even when `HELMET_PRESET` is set, because only an unset variable falls back to the preset, so an app that clears the list on purpose is not silently re-opened by the platform default.
- Security: the CSP nonce meta tag is injected only into the real `<head>`, so a literal `<head>` inside a comment, an attribute value, or a script, style, textarea or title element no longer receives it.
- Security: an HTML response that carries a CSP nonce has `public` changed to `private` and `s-maxage` dropped from its `Cache-Control`, so a shared cache cannot store a page whose nonce differs per request.
- Fixed: the Vite dev origin must be a bare origin (no path, query, fragment or userinfo) and is normalized to `scheme://host[:port]`; a CSP directive the app removed is no longer recreated by the dev origin, which dropped its `default-src` fallback (it is copied from `default-src` first, or skipped).
- Fixed: the Laravel adapter resets Vite's CSP nonce when the request ends (after the mismatch check and the nonce meta tag, on success and when the inner handler throws), so a long-lived worker (Octane, Swoole, FrankenPHP) does not carry one request's nonce into the next.
- Changed: CI pulls its Docker Hub images through the GitLab Dependency Proxy (the group's CI_DEPENDENCY_PROXY_GROUP_IMAGE_PREFIX), so pipelines no longer hit Docker Hub's anonymous pull limit.
- Docs: the README and the `Presets` docblock now state the `citadel` preset's NAT assumption: `172.18.0.1` is the Docker bridge gateway, the preset is safe only when the front proxy reaches the app over that bridge, and a published app port that is source-NATed to the gateway address would make a direct client look like the proxy, so the platform must not publish the app's port.
- Changed: docs and package metadata name nougat as the canonical repository, with git.wayne.edu and GitHub as read-only mirrors, until git.wayne.edu has CI runners.

### 0.2.6 (2026-11-02)[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#0-2-6-2026-11-02)

- Fixed: HTML rewrites (CSP nonce meta, environment ribbon) keep the response's view object, so `assertInertia()` and `assertViewHas()` work in apps that use HELMET.
- Changed: the deploy layer's Squire kit is refreshed to 0.3.3 (release options can now live in ./.env.squire).
- Changed: the deploy layer's Squire kit is refreshed to 0.3.4 (the local .env.squire file is now git-ignored).
- Docs: BEST_PRACTICES.md tags re-checked against the code; H22, H24 and H28 are now Enforced, H32 is Enforced, and the gap list line numbers are current.
- Changed: composer.json sets config.audit.abandoned to report, making the Composer audit policy explicit.
- Docs: README Docker test commands cover PHP 8.5, 8.4 and 8.3 on both PowerShell and sh, and the middleware error-path wording matches the default rethrow behaviour.

### 0.2.5 (2026-10-29)[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#0-2-5-2026-10-29)

- Added: agent-ready site (prompt blocks, Markdown twins, llms.txt), from Squire's kit.
- Added: HELMET_SESSION_SECURE=always keeps the session cookie Secure even when HTTPS is not detected.
- Changed: the proof page moves to a private site that needs a Wayne State sign-in.
- Changed: project names written as words except acronyms.
- Fixed: stale capability claims in the site and docs.

### 0.2.4 (2026-10-29)[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#0-2-4-2026-10-29)

- `HELMET_PRESET` (Laravel) now also comes from the private `waynestate/playbook` package when the environment has no value: the config reads it through `Waynestate\Helmet\Support\Setting`, which checks the environment first, then PLAYBOOK, then gives up. A missing preset is still not an error, and `waynestate/playbook` is suggested, never required. The README gains a "WSU values (PLAYBOOK)" section with the fetch commands.

### 0.2.3 (2026-10-29)[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#0-2-3-2026-10-29)

- Fixed: `helmet_boot()` removed `X-Powered-By` only after it had already answered the health check path, so a GET or HEAD to `/up` (the default `health_path`) still sent the header. The removal now runs before the health answer and the request-forgery rejection, so both early exits leave the response clean.

### 0.2.2 (2026-10-29)[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#0-2-2-2026-10-29)

- Every JSON log record now carries a request ID in `extra.request_id`: 16 lowercase hex characters generated by HELMET (`Logging::requestId()`), stamped by a processor pushed before the redaction processor, so a record with a `password` context key still comes out redacted and keeps its ID. An inbound header is never trusted for the ID. `Logging::create()` takes an optional fourth argument for a caller-supplied ID (8 to 64 letters, digits, dots, underscores or dashes; anything else is ignored), and `helmet_boot()` accepts it as `log.request_id`, which must be a string. `helmet_boot()` now also returns the ID as `request_id`.

### 0.2.1 (2026-10-29)[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#0-2-1-2026-10-29)

- Upgrade note: a raw-PHP app that still used the default `PHPSESSID` cookie gets the new `WSUSESSID` name (`__Host-WSUSESSID` on HTTPS), so signed-in users sign in once more after deploying. Laravel apps are unaffected (Laravel names its own cookie).
- Docs: added a "Running off Citadel" section to the README with a table for Citadel, OpenShift, Coolify and raw Docker behind a compose proxy: what sits in front, what to put in `HELMET_PROXIES`, and where logs go. The README log example now leads with `php://stderr`, and the hard-coded `172.18.0.1` now lives only in that table, with the other references pointing at the `citadel` preset.
- `SessionHardening::apply()` now also sets the session cookie name, lifetime, path, domain and cache limiter: `cookie_lifetime=0` (a browser-session cookie), `cache_limiter=nocache`, `cookie_path=/`, an empty `cookie_domain` (host-only), and the name `__Host-WSUSESSID` on HTTPS or `WSUSESSID` on HTTP. The rename happens only while the name is still the PHP default `PHPSESSID`; an app-chosen name is left alone, and SESAME reads whatever `session_name()` returns.

### 0.2.0 (2026-10-29)[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#0-2-0-2026-10-29)

- Fixed the `<head>` match when injecting the csp-nonce meta tag into HTML responses: the old pattern also matched `<header>` and `<headline>` and injected the tag after the wrong element. Responses that carry a `Content-Length` header now have it refreshed to the new body length after injection, so a stale length cannot cut the page off mid-tag.
- Narrowed the trusted-header set in the Laravel adapter. `X-Forwarded-Host`, `X-Forwarded-Prefix` and now `X-Forwarded-Port` are no longer trusted by default. Port is out because Citadel's HA-Proxy never sends it, so a client-sent value would pass through untouched and change the port Laravel reports and the URLs it generates. Apps that need any of them choose the set themselves with `trustProxies(at: ..., headers: ...)` or `TrustProxies::withHeaders()`.
- Laravel now agrees with HELMET on multi-value `X-Forwarded-Proto`. Citadel's HA-Proxy appends the header instead of replacing it, so a client can produce `https, http`. Symfony reads the first value of such a list (the client's), while HELMET reads the last (the one the closest proxy appended). A new middleware prepended to the global chain rewrites the header to its last value when the request comes from a trusted proxy; a single value is left alone, and requests from untrusted peers are ignored as before.
- An unknown `HELMET_PRESET` now throws even when `HELMET_PROXIES` is set. A typo in the preset name fails loudly at boot instead of going silently unused.
- Docs: noted that the CSP nonce is added to `style-src` and `style-src-elem`. A browser ignores `'unsafe-inline'` once a nonce is present, so overriding `style-src` with `["'unsafe-inline'"]` loses inline styles instead of restoring them.
- Added HSTS `preload` support. Set `hsts_preload` / `HELMET_HSTS_PRELOAD` to `true` to append the `preload` directive to the `Strict-Transport-Security` header. Preload requires a `max-age` of at least one year (31536000) and `includeSubDomains`; a shorter max-age or missing `includeSubDomains` throws. Preload is hard to undo: once a browser has preloaded the domain it refuses plain-HTTP connections until the entry is removed.
- Added Trusted Types directives on the report-only CSP header. Set `csp_trusted_types.enabled` / `HELMET_CSP_TRUSTED_TYPES_ENABLED` to `true` to append `require-trusted-types-for 'script'` and `trusted-types <policies>` to the `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only` header only (never the enforcing header). Policy names default to `["default"]`; set `csp_trusted_types.policies` / `HELMET_CSP_TRUSTED_TYPES_POLICIES` to override. Invalid policy names throw.
- Added opt-in `Cache-Control: no-store`. Set `no_store.enabled` / `HELMET_NO_STORE_ENABLED` to `true` to send `Cache-Control: no-store` on matching responses. `no_store.paths` / `HELMET_NO_STORE_PATHS` limits the header to specific path prefixes; empty means every response. An existing `Cache-Control` header is never overridden.
- Added `helmet_up()`: answers the `/up` health check with `200`, `Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8`, `Cache-Control: no-store` and the body `ok`, then exits. For a raw PHP app with no front controller, point the probe at a `public/up.php` that requires the autoloader and calls it. `helmet_boot()` now calls `helmet_up()` for the health path; behaviour is unchanged.
- Added an opt-in request-forgery (CSRF) guard. `helmet_boot()` accepts a `csrf` option, the PSR-15 core exposes `RequestForgeryGuard`, and the Laravel adapter registers a `RequestForgeryGuard` middleware when `helmet.csrf.enabled` is true. Safe methods (`GET`, `HEAD`, `OPTIONS`) always pass. For state-changing requests, `Sec-Fetch-Site` is used when present; otherwise the `Origin` header is checked against the request's own origin and `csrf.trusted_origins`. A rejected request receives `403` with `Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8`, `Cache-Control: no-store` and the body `Forbidden`. Config keys: `csrf.enabled`, `csrf.allow_same_site`, `csrf.trusted_origins`, `csrf.except`; env vars: `HELMET_CSRF_ENABLED`, `HELMET_CSRF_ALLOW_SAME_SITE`, `HELMET_CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS`, `HELMET_CSRF_EXCEPT`.
- Added configurable `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy` (COOP), `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy` (CORP) and `Permissions-Policy` headers. COOP defaults to `same-origin` (set `coop` / `HELMET_COOP` to `same-origin-allow-popups`, `noopener-allow-popups` or `unsafe-none`, or `null` to send no header). CORP is opt-in (set `corp` / `HELMET_CORP` to `same-site`, `same-origin` or `cross-origin`). Permissions-Policy defaults to a deny list for `camera`, `geolocation`, `microphone`, `payment` and `usb` (set `permissions_policy` / `HELMET_PERMISSIONS_POLICY` to a feature map; an empty map sends no header). Invalid values throw.
- BEST_PRACTICES tags brought up to date. The Stack lines are now picture perfect.
- PHPStan and Pint now run from Pinstripe, the stack's coding standard, instead of a hand copy. `composer.json` requires `waynestate/pinstripe` (dev-main, until 0.1.0 is tagged) as a dev dependency, `phpstan.neon` includes `vendor/waynestate/pinstripe/phpstan/raw.neon` (keeping this repo's paths, PHP version range and three commented exceptions), and `pint.json` keeps the `per` preset Pinstripe ships. No behaviour change; the code is just cut from the same cloth now.

- First tagged release.

Source: https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/advisor.html

## Use HELMET from your coding agent (ADVISOR)[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/advisor.html#use-helmet-from-your-coding-agent-advisor)

This page is for developers whose coding agent runs [ADVISOR](https://github.com/waynestate/advisor), the stack's read-only MCP server. HELMET ships an ADVISOR module, so the agent can ask HELMET two questions without leaving its sandbox: "which headers does HELMET send, and why?" and "how long is this app's PHP floor supported?" Both answers come from HELMET's own code. Next, see [The headers](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/headers.html) for the same ground in prose and [Customizing the CSP](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/csp.html) for changing it.

### Install ADVISOR[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/advisor.html#install-advisor)

In the app, install ADVISOR as a dev dependency:

```bash
composer require --dev waynestate/advisor
```

Then add one line to the app's `modules.json` (or point `ADVISOR_MODULES_FILE` at a file that holds it):

```json
{
    "modules": [
        "Waynestate\\Helmet\\Advisor\\HelmetModule"
    ]
}
```

HELMET does not require ADVISOR, and ADVISOR does not require HELMET: the module only loads when both are installed and `modules.json` names it.

### The two read-only tools[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/advisor.html#the-two-read-only-tools)

Both tools take exactly one argument, `path`: the app folder, inside the project root (default: the root itself). Both run in-process: no subprocess, no network, nothing written. Neither reads `.env`, the environment or any secret.

#### helmet_headers[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/advisor.html#helmet-headers)

`helmet_headers` builds the headers HELMET sends with its defaults, through the same `SecurityHeaders::build()` every consumer path uses, and returns:

- `headers`: each header with its exact value, when it is sent (Strict-Transport-Security goes on HTTPS responses only) and the reason it is there.
- `csp.directives`: each Content-Security-Policy directive with its sources and its reason. The per-request nonce shows as `PerRequestNonce`, because a real one only exists inside a request.
- `removed` and `optional`: `X-Powered-By`, which `helmet_boot()` strips, and the headers that are off until you turn them on (Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy, Reporting-Endpoints, `Cache-Control: no-store`, report-only mode).
- `wiring`: what the app folder says about HELMET. The version `composer.lock` pins, whether it is a Laravel app, whether `config/helmet.php` is published and still matches the copy HELMET ships, and which front controller calls `helmet_boot()`. Each note names the file it came from.
- `settings`: every `HELMET_` variable (and the matching `helmet_boot()` key) that changes the answer. The tool lists them; it never reads their values.

One directive, as it comes back:

```json
{
    "directive": "base-uri",
    "sources": ["'self'"],
    "reason": "Stops an injected <base> tag from re-pointing every relative URL on the page; default-src does not cover it."
}
```

The reasons live in `src/Headers/HeaderReasons.php`, next to the policy they explain, and a test fails when a header or directive is added without one.

#### helmet_php_support[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/advisor.html#helmet-php-support)

`helmet_php_support` reads `require.php` and `config.platform.php` from the app's `composer.json`, takes the lowest PHP version the constraint allows (the floor), and looks it up in the CREED `policy.json` that ADVISOR bundles. It reads the policy with HELMET's own `JsonFilePolicySource` and `VersionStatus`, the code behind the environment ribbon and the PHP support metrics, so all three agree. It returns:

- `floor`: the version, its status (`active`, `security`, `eol` or `unknown`), its active and security dates, the days of security support left, and the ribbon's own warning text.
- `platform_pin`: the same for `config.platform.php`, when the app sets one.
- `allowed`: every PHP version in the policy that the constraint allows, each with its status.
- `summary`: one sentence to repeat to a person, for example "The floor, PHP 8.3 (from ^8.3), is security-only: fixes stop on 2027-12-31 (419 days)."
- `source`: the policy file and the date CREED refreshed it, the date ADVISOR bundled it, and the date the answer is for.

A missing constraint, one with no lower bound (`*`) and one Composer cannot parse are each explained, never guessed. A folder with no `composer.json` is refused.

Note

HELMET reports; PROCTOR decides. Every answer names its source and says plainly what ran, and PROCTOR's check against the same CREED policy is what passes or fails a build. A helmet tells you where the hits will land; it does not referee the game.

---

Source: https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/cross-origin-isolation.html

## Cross-origin isolation and feature policy[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/cross-origin-isolation.html#cross-origin-isolation-and-feature-policy)

This page covers the three headers that round out the baseline beyond the CSP: `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy`, `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy` and `Permissions-Policy`. Two are on by default, one is opt-in. When you are done here, see [The headers](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/headers.html) for the full set.

### Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/cross-origin-isolation.html#cross-origin-opener-policy)

`Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy` defaults to `same-origin`, which puts the page in its own browsing-context group so an opener or parent page cannot read it. Set `coop` (raw PHP) or `HELMET_COOP` (Laravel) to `same-origin-allow-popups` or `noopener-allow-popups` to keep the isolation but let a popup window (such as an OAuth login popup to the IdP) stay cross-origin, or to `unsafe-none` to turn the header off. Set it to `null` to send no COOP header at all.

### Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/cross-origin-isolation.html#cross-origin-resource-policy)

`Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy` is opt-in: HELMET sends no CORP header by default, because a blanket `same-site` can break an app whose assets are read cross-origin. Set `corp` (raw PHP) or `HELMET_CORP` (Laravel) to `same-site`, `same-origin` or `cross-origin` to send it.

### Permissions-Policy[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/cross-origin-isolation.html#permissions-policy)

`Permissions-Policy` defaults to a deny list: `camera`, `geolocation`, `microphone`, `payment` and `usb` are all denied, so an injected script cannot use a feature the page has switched off. Set `permissions_policy` (raw PHP) or `HELMET_PERMISSIONS_POLICY` (Laravel) to a feature map to change it: each feature maps to an allowlist of `self` and https origins, and an empty allowlist denies the feature. An empty map sends no Permissions-Policy header.

### Example[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/cross-origin-isolation.html#example)

```php
$helmet = helmet_boot([
    'preset' => 'citadel',
    'coop' => 'same-origin-allow-popups',
    'corp' => 'same-site',
    'permissions_policy' => [
        'camera' => ['self'],
        'geolocation' => [],
    ],
]);
```

### Settings[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/cross-origin-isolation.html#settings)

| Setting | Raw PHP (`helmet_boot()`) | Laravel |
| --- | --- | --- |
| COOP | `coop` | `HELMET_COOP` / `helmet.coop`, default `same-origin`, `null` sends no header |
| CORP | `corp` | `HELMET_CORP` / `helmet.corp`, default `null` (no header) |
| Permissions-Policy | `permissions_policy` | `HELMET_PERMISSIONS_POLICY` / `helmet.permissions_policy`, default deny list, `[]` sends no header |

### Validation[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/cross-origin-isolation.html#validation)

An invalid COOP or CORP value, or a Permissions-Policy feature name or allowlist entry that is not `self` or an https origin, throws, so a typo fails loudly instead of sending a header the browser will ignore.

### Related[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/cross-origin-isolation.html#related)

- [The headers](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/headers.html)
- [Customizing the CSP](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/csp.html)
- [Configuring HSTS](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/hsts.html)
- [Raw PHP](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-raw-php.html)
- [Laravel](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-laravel.html)
- [Environment variables](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html)

Source: https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/csp.html

## Customizing the CSP[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/csp.html#customizing-the-csp)

The default policy is a starting point, not a cage. Pass a `csp` policy (raw PHP) or a second constructor argument (middleware) and it is merged over the default, per directive: a directive you set replaces the default's value for that directive, and a directive you leave out keeps the default. The default itself, exactly as the code defines it, is on [The headers](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/headers.html).

### Merging over the default[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/csp.html#merging-over-the-default)

To remove a directive the default sets, set it to `null`:

```php
$helmet = helmet_boot([
    'preset' => 'citadel',
    'csp' => [
        // Replace the default img-src.
        'img-src' => ["'self'", 'data:'],
        // Remove form-action entirely.
        'form-action' => null,
    ],
]);
```

In Laravel the same array goes in `helmet.csp` (published config) or `HELMET_CSP` (JSON in the environment); see [Laravel](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-laravel.html). The merge rule is identical on both paths, because both call the same core function.

### Reporting setup[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/csp.html#reporting-setup)

By default the policy is enforced: a violation is blocked. To see what would be blocked before you enforce it, or to keep collecting reports after you do, point the policy at a report endpoint.

Set `csp_report_uri` (raw PHP) or `HELMET_CSP_REPORT_URI` (Laravel) to the URL browsers POST reports to. It must be `https`. HELMET then adds `report-uri` and `report-to` to the policy and sends a `Reporting-Endpoints` header naming the endpoint. Set `csp_report_only` (or `HELMET_CSP_REPORT_ONLY`) to `true` to send the policy as `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only`, which observes violations without blocking them.

```php
$helmet = helmet_boot([
    'preset' => 'citadel',
    'csp_report_uri' => 'https://app.example.edu/csp-report',
    'csp_report_only' => true,
]);
```

Warning

An invalid URI (not `https`, no host, or a value carrying whitespace or a quote) throws at boot, so a typo fails loudly instead of pointing the browser at a destination it cannot reach.

Tip

Run report-only first. That is how you see what would be blocked before you enforce it; once the policy is clean, switch off `csp_report_only` and keep collecting.

### Receiving the reports in Laravel[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/csp.html#receiving-the-reports-in-laravel)

Laravel ships an opt-in endpoint that receives the reports and logs one line per violation (the violated directive, the blocked URI's host, and the document path) and nothing else. It accepts both report formats: the legacy `application/csp-report` object, and the Reporting API's `application/reports+json` array, from which it logs the `csp-violation` entries (at most 20 per POST; browsers batch other report types into the same request, and those are ignored). The route is off until you register it:

```php
// routes/web.php
Route::cspReport();                 // POST /csp-report
Route::cspReport('/reports/csp');   // or your own path
```

The endpoint caps the body at 16 KiB, returns `204`, and carries no authentication of its own; wrap it in your own middleware if you want to keep it private. Browsers POST reports without a CSRF token, so the route excludes the `web` group's CSRF middleware. Because the endpoint is public and its input is attacker-influenced, it is throttled by default to 60 reports a minute per IP (`throttle:60,1`); pass a second argument to use a different throttle, or `null` to disable it:

```php
Route::cspReport('/reports/csp', 'throttle:120,1'); // your own limit
Route::cspReport('/reports/csp', null);             // no throttle
```

### Related[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/csp.html#related)

- [The headers](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/headers.html)
- [Laravel](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-laravel.html)
- [Raw PHP](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-raw-php.html)
- [PSR-15 middleware](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-psr15.html)
- [Environment variables](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html)

Source: https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/csrf.html

## The request-forgery guard[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/csrf.html#the-request-forgery-guard)

This page is for the opt-in request-forgery (CSRF) guard: the rule HELMET applies to state-changing requests before they reach the app, and how to turn it on in raw PHP, PSR-15 and Laravel. Read it before you enable the guard, then wire it up in the section that matches your stack.

`SameSite=Lax` is a layer, not a wall. The guard is the second layer: it checks the request, and if the check fails the request never reaches your code.

### The goal[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/csrf.html#the-goal)

Turn the guard on and let the same rule run on every consumer path. The guard is off by default; when it is on, it is the same rule on every consumer path, because the raw PHP path and the Laravel adapter both call the one `allows()` decision in `Waynestate\Helmet\Csrf\RequestForgeryGuard`.

### The rule[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/csrf.html#the-rule)

For `GET`, `HEAD` and `OPTIONS` the request passes. Those are the only methods in `SAFE_METHODS`. For anything else:

1. `Sec-Fetch-Site` is the primary signal when the browser sends it. `same-origin` and `none` pass, `same-site` passes only when `allow_same_site` is true, and `cross-site` or an unknown value is rejected.
2. When `Sec-Fetch-Site` is absent, the `Origin` header is checked against the request's own origin and `trusted_origins`. `Origin: null` is rejected, an unparseable origin is rejected, and an absent origin passes, because a non-browser client authenticates some other way.
3. A path in `except` skips the guard. A pattern is an exact path, a prefix ending in `*`, or `*` for every path.

The request's own origin comes from `HTTP_HOST` plus the same trusted-proxy HTTPS decision the security headers use, so a spoofed `X-Forwarded-Proto` from an untrusted peer cannot change the origin. Origins are compared in canonical form: lowercase `scheme://host:port`, with the default port dropped (`443` for https, `80` for http), and user info, a query, a fragment, or a path all rejected, so a URL with a path cannot silently become an origin.

### The rejection answer[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/csrf.html#the-rejection-answer)

A rejected request receives `403`, `Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8`, `Cache-Control: no-store` and the body `Forbidden`. The answer never echoes request headers.

When a logger is set, a refused request is also logged as the `helmet.request_refused` security event. Its context carries `event` (`request_refused`), `method` (upper case), `path` (no query string), `sec_fetch_site` (`same-origin`, `same-site`, `cross-site`, `none`, `other`, or null when the header is absent), and `origin_present` (bool). It never carries the Origin value, cookies, Authorization, or any other header value, and a logger that throws never changes the `403` answer.

### Raw PHP[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/csrf.html#raw-php)

```php
$helmet = helmet_boot([
    'preset' => 'citadel',
    'csrf' => [
        'enabled' => true,
        'allow_same_site' => false,
        'trusted_origins' => ['https://forms.example.edu'],
        'except' => ['/api/webhooks/*'],
    ],
]);
```

`helmet_boot()` runs the check after the health path and before the security headers. A rejected request stops there.

### PSR-15[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/csrf.html#psr-15)

```php
use Waynestate\Helmet\Csrf\RequestForgeryGuard;

$guard = new RequestForgeryGuard(
    $proxies,
    $factory,
    $factory,
    false,
    ['https://forms.example.edu'],
    ['/api/webhooks/*'],
);
```

The guard needs the PSR-17 response and stream factories only when it rejects a request. A PSR-15 user passes a `LoggerInterface` as the last constructor argument `$logger` to log refusals.

Note

The constructor validates its configuration. A trusted origin that is not a valid `http` or `https` origin, or an `except` pattern that is not a non-empty string, throws `InvalidArgumentException` at construction, so a typo fails loudly instead of letting a forged request through.

### Laravel[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/csrf.html#laravel)

Set the config or the environment:

```
HELMET_CSRF_ENABLED=true
HELMET_CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS=https://forms.example.edu
HELMET_CSRF_EXCEPT=/api/webhooks/*
```

The provider registers the `RequestForgeryGuard` middleware in the `web` group only when `helmet.csrf.enabled` is true. It calls the same core rule, so a Laravel app and a raw PHP app with the same settings make the same decision.

### Related[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/csrf.html#related)

- [The session](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/session.html)
- [Metrics](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/metrics.html)

---

Source: https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/headers.html

## The headers[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/headers.html#the-headers)

Every response gets the same set, built by one shared function. This page shows the set, the default Content-Security-Policy exactly as the code defines it, and the rule behind each header. To change the policy itself, see [Customizing the CSP](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/csp.html).

![A chalkboard play of HELMET's default headers. Seven O's on the line of scrimmage each run a route to one header: Content-Security-Policy (default-src 'self'; base-uri 'self'; object-src 'none'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'self', plus 7 more directives, a fresh nonce and 'strict-dynamic'), X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN, Referrer-Policy strict-origin-when-cross-origin, Permissions-Policy camera=(), geolocation=(), microphone=(), payment=(), usb=(), Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy same-origin, and Strict-Transport-Security max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains on HTTPS responses only. Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy is on the bench, opt-in. The HELMET mark sits in the pocket.](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/play.svg)

The play is read from `src/Headers/SecurityHeaders.php`: seven routes, one per default header, drawn in the order HELMET sets them. Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy waits on the bench until you opt in. With reduced motion on, you get the finished play.

### The set[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/headers.html#the-set)

| Header | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `Content-Security-Policy` | the WayneUI default policy, plus a per-request nonce and `strict-dynamic` |
| `X-Content-Type-Options` | `nosniff` |
| `X-Frame-Options` | `SAMEORIGIN` |
| `Referrer-Policy` | `strict-origin-when-cross-origin` |
| `Permissions-Policy` | `camera=(), geolocation=(), microphone=(), payment=(), usb=()` by default, configurable |
| `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy` | `same-origin` by default, configurable, `null` sends no header |
| `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy` | not sent by default, opt-in |
| `Strict-Transport-Security` | `max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains` by default, HTTPS only, configurable |

The default CSP is the union of the WayneUI recipes, with `frame-ancestors 'self'`, `base-uri 'self'`, `object-src 'none'` and `form-action 'self'` added so an app can never be framed by a stranger, have its base tag hijacked, load plugins, or post its forms to an attacker. `script-src` carries a per-request nonce plus `strict-dynamic`, so a script loaded with the nonce can load other scripts without opening the door to `'unsafe-inline'`.

Milquetoast is a Helmet song. It is not a Content-Security-Policy.

### The default policy, exactly[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/headers.html#the-default-policy-exactly)

`SecurityHeaders::defaultCspPolicy()` returns the full default, directive by directive:

| Directive | Sources |
| --- | --- |
| `default-src` | `'self'` |
| `style-src` | `'self'`, `https://wayneui.apps.wayne.edu` |
| `style-src-attr` | `'unsafe-inline'` |
| `style-src-elem` | `'self'`, `https://wayneui.apps.wayne.edu` |
| `script-src` | `'self'`, `https://wayneui.apps.wayne.edu` |
| `font-src` | `'self'`, `data:`, `https://wayneui.apps.wayne.edu` |
| `img-src` | `'self'`, `data:`, `https://wayneui.apps.wayne.edu` |
| `connect-src` | `'self'`, `https://wayneui.apps.wayne.edu` |
| `base-uri` | `'self'` |
| `object-src` | `'none'` |
| `form-action` | `'self'` |
| `frame-ancestors` | `'self'` |

Where each piece comes from:

- `default-src`, `style-src`, `style-src-attr`, `script-src`, `font-src`, `img-src` and `connect-src` come from the raw PHP recipe.
- `style-src-elem` comes from the Laravel/Blade recipe. It does not carry `'unsafe-inline'`; only `style-src-attr` does, and only for the inline `style="..."` attributes the recipes rely on (block spacing). `style-src-attr` governs only the style attribute, not `<style>` elements or stylesheets, so this is the narrowest allowance that keeps those recipes working.
- `frame-ancestors 'self'` covers clickjacking at the CSP layer.
- `base-uri 'self'`, `object-src 'none'` and `form-action 'self'` close the base-tag, plugin and form-targeting gaps that `default-src` alone does not cover in every browser.
- `data:` appears on `font-src` and `img-src`: Vite and Vue inline small fonts as `data:` URIs, and the nonce does not cover font sources.

### The nonce[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/headers.html#the-nonce)

`SecurityHeaders::generateNonce()` makes a new nonce for every request: 18 random bytes, base64 encoded. When the header is built, the nonce is bound to `script-src`, and to `style-src` and `style-src-elem` when those directives are present in the merged policy. An app may remove a directive with `null`, so the nonce only goes on the directives that are there. Vite and Vue inject `<style>` and `<link>` tags that carry the nonce, which is why the style directives need it too.

`strict-dynamic` rides along on `script-src`: it lets a script that was loaded with the nonce load other scripts dynamically, without opening `script-src` to `'unsafe-inline'`.

### Permissions-Policy[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/headers.html#permissions-policy)

The default denies the browser features a typical app never uses: `camera`, `geolocation`, `microphone`, `payment` and `usb`. An injected script cannot use a feature the page has disabled, so the deny list targets the features most useful to an attacker and least useful to a form-filling app. `interest-cohort` is not in it: the browser vendors dropped it, so denying it buys nothing.

The header renders as `feature=(allowlist)`: an empty list denies the feature, `self` allows the page's own origin unquoted, and an https origin is quoted. Passing `null` (the default) uses the deny list above; an empty map sends no `Permissions-Policy` header at all.

### Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy and Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/headers.html#cross-origin-opener-policy-and-cross-origin-resource-policy)

COOP puts the page in its own browsing context group, so a cross-origin page cannot reach it through `window.opener` or the cross-origin Web APIs. The default is `same-origin`: only same-origin pages may open it. The accepted values are `unsafe-none`, `same-origin-allow-popups`, `same-origin` and `noopener-allow-popups`; anything else throws. Set COOP to `null` to send no header.

CORP declares who may load this page's resources cross-origin. It is the resource-side half of the cross-origin isolation pair with COOP, and its accepted values are `same-site`, `same-origin` and `cross-origin`. CORP is off by default: pass a value to send it. See [Cross-origin isolation and feature policy](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/cross-origin-isolation.html) for the pair working together.

### Strict-Transport-Security[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/headers.html#strict-transport-security)

The default is `max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains` (one year, all subdomains), sent on HTTPS responses only. Roll it out in stages: start with a short `max-age`, raise it once nothing breaks, and keep `includeSubDomains` only when every subdomain serves HTTPS.

`preload` is a decision for the domain owner, not for one app, so HELMET never adds it by default. It is opt-in, and it is only appended when the `max-age` is at least a year and `includeSubDomains` is on, because a browser refuses a preload HSTS header that does not meet both. A negative `max-age` throws. The knobs and the staged rollout are on [Configuring HSTS](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/hsts.html).

### One shared function[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/headers.html#one-shared-function)

`SecurityHeaders` is the single place that defines HELMET's security headers and the default Content-Security-Policy. Both the PSR-15 middleware and the framework-free `helmet_boot()` path build their headers from this class, so the two consumer paths always agree. That is what lets the [Laravel](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-laravel.html) and [Raw PHP](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-raw-php.html) pages promise identical behavior: they call the same `build()`.

### Related[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/headers.html#related)

- [Customizing the CSP](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/csp.html)
- [Configuring HSTS](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/hsts.html)
- [Cross-origin isolation and feature policy](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/cross-origin-isolation.html)
- [Laravel](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-laravel.html)
- [Raw PHP](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-raw-php.html)
- [PSR-15 middleware](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-psr15.html)
- [API](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.html)
- [Troubleshooting](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html)

Source: https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/hsts.html

## Configuring HSTS[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/hsts.html#configuring-hsts)

This page is for tuning the `Strict-Transport-Security` header: what it sends by default, how to roll it out in stages, and the exact options on each consumer path. When you are done here, move on to [The headers](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/headers.html) for the rest of the baseline.

### The default[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/hsts.html#the-default)

The default is `max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains` (one year, all subdomains), sent on HTTPS responses only. A request that was not really secure never carries the header, because HELMET decides HTTPS from the trusted proxy list; see [HTTPS, and why the proxy list matters](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/https-and-proxies.html).

### Roll it out in stages[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/hsts.html#roll-it-out-in-stages)

Roll it out in stages: start with a short `max-age`, raise it once nothing breaks, and keep `includeSubDomains` only when every subdomain serves HTTPS.

### Raw PHP[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/hsts.html#raw-php)

Set `hsts_max_age` (seconds) and `hsts_include_subdomains` (raw PHP):

```php
$helmet = helmet_boot([
    'preset' => 'citadel',
    'hsts_max_age' => 600,
    'hsts_include_subdomains' => false,
]);
```

### Middleware and Laravel[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/hsts.html#middleware-and-laravel)

In the PSR-15 middleware, pass the last two constructor arguments of `SecurityHeadersMiddleware`. In Laravel, use the environment variables below; the config keys are `helmet.hsts`, `helmet.hsts_include_subdomains` and `helmet.hsts_preload`.

| Variable | Config key | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `HELMET_HSTS_MAX_AGE` | `helmet.hsts` | `31536000` | The HSTS `max-age` in seconds, sent on HTTPS only. It must not be negative. |
| `HELMET_HSTS_INCLUDE_SUBDOMAINS` | `helmet.hsts_include_subdomains` | `true` | Set `false` to omit the HSTS `includeSubDomains` directive. |
| `HELMET_HSTS_PRELOAD` | `helmet.hsts_preload` | `false` | Set `true` to append the `preload` directive to HSTS. Requires `max-age` of at least one year and `includeSubDomains`. Preload is hard to undo: once a browser has preloaded the domain it refuses plain-HTTP connections until the entry is removed. |

### Preload[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/hsts.html#preload)

`preload` is a decision for the domain owner, not for one app, so HELMET never adds it by default. If your domain is in the preload list, set `HELMET_HSTS_PRELOAD=true` (or `hsts_preload` in raw PHP) with a `max-age` of at least one year and `includeSubDomains`; a shorter `max-age` or missing `includeSubDomains` throws.

Warning

Preload is hard to undo: once a browser has preloaded the domain it refuses plain-HTTP connections until the entry is removed.

### Check the header[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/hsts.html#check-the-header)

Ask for a response over HTTPS and look at the header line:

```
curl -sI https://app.example.edu/
```

Expected: `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains` by default, or the value you configured. The same request over plain HTTP carries no HSTS header.

### Related[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/hsts.html#related)

- [The headers](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/headers.html)
- [Customizing the CSP](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/csp.html)
- [HTTPS, and why the proxy list matters](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/https-and-proxies.html)
- [Platform presets](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/platform-presets.html)
- [Running off Citadel](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/running-off-citadel.html)
- [Environment variables](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html)

Source: https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/https-and-proxies.html

## HTTPS, and why the proxy list matters[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/https-and-proxies.html#https-and-why-the-proxy-list-matters)

This page explains how HELMET decides whether a request really arrived over HTTPS, and why the trusted proxy list is the load-bearing part of that decision. When you understand it, pick your list on [Platform presets](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/platform-presets.html) or [Running off Citadel](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/running-off-citadel.html).

Citadel sits behind HA-Proxy, so the PHP process sees the proxy's address, not the client's, and the real scheme arrives in `X-Forwarded-Proto`. HELMET only honors that header when the connection came from a trusted proxy. A spoofed `X-Forwarded-Proto: https` from the public internet is ignored, and no HSTS header is sent for a request that was not really secure.

The proxy check is the Unsung hero of the headers. Nobody notices it until a forged `X-Forwarded-Proto` walks in and gets nowhere.

### How the scheme is decided[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/https-and-proxies.html#how-the-scheme-is-decided)

`HttpsDetector` makes the decision from the raw `$_SERVER` array, so it works identically in the framework-free boot path and in any adapter:

1. If the SAPI reports TLS (the `HTTPS` key is set and not `off`), the request is HTTPS. This is the only signal trusted unconditionally.
2. Otherwise, the request is HTTPS only when the peer (`REMOTE_ADDR`) is a trusted proxy and the forwarded `X-Forwarded-Proto` is `https`.

A comma-separated `X-Forwarded-Proto` list keeps one rule everywhere: the last non-empty value wins, because it is the one the closest proxy appended. Values are trimmed and lower-cased, and empty tokens are ignored, so a trailing comma cannot hide the real value.

### What the proxy list accepts[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/https-and-proxies.html#what-the-proxy-list-accepts)

`TrustedProxies` takes exact IPv4 or IPv6 addresses and IPv4 or IPv6 CIDR ranges. Every entry is validated at construction time, so bad config fails loudly at boot instead of looking like working config while trusting nothing, or the wrong thing:

- An entry that is not a valid address or CIDR throws.
- A `/0` prefix (which would trust every address of its family) is refused.
- The wildcard `*` is refused.

The matching itself is delegated to Symfony's `IpUtils`, maintained security code; the class only validates the config. An IPv4-mapped IPv6 address (`::ffff:a.b.c.d`) is unmapped to `a.b.c.d` before matching, so a dual-stack peer presenting its IPv4 address in mapped form still matches an IPv4 entry in the list. An empty list trusts nothing.

### What happens with no list[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/https-and-proxies.html#what-happens-with-no-list)

With neither a preset nor a list, no address is trusted, so forwarded headers such as `X-Forwarded-Proto` are ignored and the request is read as it arrived. An explicitly empty `HELMET_PROXIES=` means trust nobody, even when a preset is set; only an unset variable falls back to the preset. An unknown preset name throws at boot, so a typo fails loudly instead of silently trusting nothing.

Warning

List only the address the front proxy connects from, never a whole private range. A broad range such as `10.0.0.0/8` also trusts other containers on the same network, and any of them could then set `X-Forwarded-Proto`.

When the list does hold a broad entry, an IPv4 range shorter than `/16` or an IPv6 range shorter than `/48`, HELMET writes one `helmet.broad_trusted_proxy` warning at boot so the range is hard to miss in the logs. Set `HELMET_WARN_BROAD_PROXIES=false` (or pass `warn_broad_proxies: false` to `helmet_boot()`) once you have reviewed the range and accepted it.

### Resolving the client IP[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/https-and-proxies.html#resolving-the-client-ip)

The same trust list drives `ClientIp::resolve()`. When the peer is a trusted proxy, the client IP is read from `X-Forwarded-For` right to left (closest proxy first), and the walk stops at the first untrusted hop, so a client-chosen entry behind that hop can never be returned. Two failure rules keep it honest:

- **Fails closed.** An unparseable entry (for example `203.0.113.5:443`) ends the walk: the peer is returned instead of walking on to an earlier, client-chosen entry.
- **Reports without quoting the attacker.** Each rejection logs one `helmet.forwarded_for_rejected` warning with `event`, `reason` (`unparseable_entry`) and `peer` in the context. The `X-Forwarded-For` header and the bad entry are never logged.

IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses are unmapped for both the peer and the forwarded entries, so a dual-stack proxy still matches its IPv4 entry instead of slipping past the trust check. The metrics endpoint uses the same list through `IpAllowList`, which applies the same validation rules to `HELMET_METRICS_ALLOW`.

### Where to set it[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/https-and-proxies.html#where-to-set-it)

Raw PHP passes the list as `trusted_proxies` (or a `preset` name) to `helmet_boot()`; Laravel reads `HELMET_PROXIES` (comma-separated), which wins over `HELMET_PRESET`. Per-platform values live in [Running off Citadel](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/running-off-citadel.html), and the presets themselves in [Platform presets](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/platform-presets.html).

### Related[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/https-and-proxies.html#related)

- [Platform presets](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/platform-presets.html)
- [Running off Citadel](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/running-off-citadel.html)
- [Configuring HSTS](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/hsts.html)
- [The session](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/session.html)
- [Metrics](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/metrics.html)
- [Environment variables](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html)

## Metrics[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/metrics.html#metrics)

This page is for the opt-in Prometheus metrics endpoint: what it reports, how to turn it on for one site, how to gate it, where request counts are kept, and how to graph the result in Grafana. Read it before you expose `/metrics`.

HELMET can expose a Prometheus metrics endpoint. It is off by default and stays off until you turn it on. HELMET does not write the exposition format by hand: it uses [promphp/prometheus_client_php](https://github.com/PromPHP/prometheus_client_php) and keeps its own layer to naming, label bounding and access control.

### The goal[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/metrics.html#the-goal)

One endpoint per app that answers three questions for a fleet dashboard: is it up, is it current (PHP and HELMET versions, and how long until its PHP release loses security support), and how is it doing (requests, latency, errors and CSP violations). Labels never carry personal data or raw paths, so the number of series stays small no matter what the internet sends.

### What it reports[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/metrics.html#what-it-reports)

| Metric | Type | Labels | Needs a store |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `helmet_info` | gauge, always 1 | `php_version`, `helmet_version` | no |
| `wsu_stack_info` | gauge, always 1 | `package`, `version` (each installed `waynestate/*` package) | no |
| `helmet_php_version_status` | gauge, 1 for the current status | `status` (`active`, `security`, `eol`, `unknown`) | no, needs a policy |
| `helmet_php_eol_timestamp_seconds` | gauge | `php_minor` (for example `8.5`) | no, needs a policy |
| `helmet_metrics_storage_up` | gauge, 1 or 0 | none | only shown when a store is set |
| `helmet_http_request_duration_seconds` | histogram (`_bucket`, `_sum`, `_count`) | `route`, `method`, `status` | yes |
| `helmet_csp_violations_total` | counter | `directive` | yes |

The first four are built fresh on every scrape, so they need nothing shared between PHP workers. The last two count across requests and need a store (see [Pick a store](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/metrics.html#pick-a-store)).

The policy is the CREED `policy.json` (set `HELMET_POLICY_PATH`). Status is looked up by PHP major and minor version, so PHP 8.5.12 reads the `8.5` entry. The end-of-support date is exposed as a Unix timestamp, which is the Prometheus way; the dashboard turns it into days.

#### How labels stay small[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/metrics.html#how-labels-stay-small)

HELMET bounds every label before it reaches the store, and anything it will not accept becomes `other`:

- `route` is a **route group the app names**, never the raw path. Laravel apps get the route name, else the URI template (`users/{user}`), else `unmatched` (a request no route took, usually a 404). Raw PHP apps pass their own group. Values must be lowercase letters, digits and `. _ / { } : -`, 64 characters at most.
- `method` is one of the standard HTTP verbs, else `OTHER`.
- `status` is the class (`2xx`, `3xx`, `4xx`, `5xx`), never the exact code.
- `directive` is a CSP Level 3 directive name, else `other`, so a forged report cannot mint a new series.

The request count is the histogram's `_count` series; there is no separate counter to keep in sync.

### Enable it[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/metrics.html#enable-it)

| Variable | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `HELMET_METRICS_ENABLED` | `true` turns the endpoint on. Off when unset. |
| `HELMET_METRICS_TOKEN` | A bearer token. The scraper sends `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Compared with `hash_equals`. |
| `HELMET_METRICS_ALLOW` | Comma-separated IPs or CIDR ranges allowed to scrape without a token. |
| `HELMET_METRICS_STORAGE` | `apcu`, `redis` or `sqlite` turns on request and CSP metrics. Unset means version and policy gauges only. |
| `HELMET_METRICS_REDIS_URL` | `redis://[:password@]host[:port][/db]` when the store is `redis`. |
| `HELMET_METRICS_SQLITE_PATH` | The database file when the store is `sqlite`. Defaults to `helmet-metrics.sqlite` in the system temp directory. |
| `HELMET_POLICY_PATH` | Path to a CREED `policy.json`, for the PHP support status and end-of-support gauges. |

Warning

With neither a token nor an allow list set, the endpoint returns `404` and logs a warning, so a misconfigured app does not hand its metrics to the whole network.

The token is read from the `Authorization` header wherever the server puts it: `HTTP_AUTHORIZATION`, `REDIRECT_HTTP_AUTHORIZATION`, or the request headers themselves. That last one matters on Apache with mod_php, which keeps the header out of `$_SERVER`.

### Pick a store[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/metrics.html#pick-a-store)

PHP shares nothing between requests, so a request counter kept in memory would count to 1 and vanish. Request and CSP metrics need a store that every worker in the app can reach. HELMET does not pick one for you.

| Store | Use it when | Limits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `apcu` | The app runs under PHP-FPM or Apache mod_php with the APCu extension. Fastest. | Per server: each container or VM counts on its own (Prometheus sums them). Lost on restart. Not shared with the CLI. Needs `ext-apcu`. |
| `redis` | Several containers serve one app, or the counts should survive a restart. | Needs `ext-redis` and a Redis the app can reach. A slow Redis adds its round trip to every request. |
| `sqlite` | No APCu and no Redis, for example a stock PHP Apache image. | Per server, like APCu. Every request takes a short write lock, so it suits small and medium traffic, not a busy API. A file in the temp directory is lost with the container. Needs `ext-pdo_sqlite`. |

Counters that reset on restart are fine: Prometheus's `rate()` and `increase()` handle resets. If the store breaks, the page still renders: the failure is logged once per request (`metrics_storage_unusable` or `metrics_record_failed`), the version gauges keep answering, and `helmet_metrics_storage_up` drops to `0` so the dashboard shows it.

### Turn it on for one site[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/metrics.html#turn-it-on-for-one-site)

#### Laravel[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/metrics.html#laravel)

Set the variables, then register the routes you want. Nothing is created until you call the macro:

```dotenv
HELMET_METRICS_ENABLED=true
HELMET_METRICS_TOKEN=<a long random string, from your secret store>
HELMET_METRICS_STORAGE=apcu
HELMET_POLICY_PATH=/path/to/creed/policy.json
```

```php
// routes/web.php
Route::helmetMetrics();                             // GET /metrics, throttle:60,1
Route::helmetMetrics('/metrics', 'throttle:120,1'); // your own throttle
Route::cspReport();                                 // POST /csp-report, counts violations by directive
```

With `HELMET_METRICS_STORAGE` set, the provider adds a terminable middleware to the front of the global stack, so it times the whole request (including your other middleware) and records after the response has been sent. Without it the middleware is not registered at all. The controller reads `helmet.metrics` from the published config and resolves the client IP through the same trusted-proxy list the headers use.

#### Raw PHP[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/metrics.html#raw-php)

Put this at the top of the front controller, after the autoloader:

```php
use function Waynestate\Helmet\helmet_metrics;
use function Waynestate\Helmet\helmet_metrics_env;
use function Waynestate\Helmet\helmet_metrics_track;

$config = helmet_metrics_env();   // reads HELMET_METRICS_* and HELMET_POLICY_PATH
$path = parse_url($_SERVER['REQUEST_URI'] ?? '/', PHP_URL_PATH) ?: '/';

if ($path === '/metrics') {
    $result = helmet_metrics(['preset' => 'citadel'] + $config);
    http_response_code($result['status']);
    header('Content-Type: ' . $result['content_type']);
    echo $result['body'];
    exit;
}

// Name the route group yourself; never pass the raw path.
$group = str_starts_with($path, '/reports') ? 'reports' : 'page';
helmet_metrics_track($config)->route($group);
```

`helmet_metrics_track()` starts the clock at `REQUEST_TIME_FLOAT` and records once at shutdown, so a page that ends with `exit` is still counted, with whatever status code it sent. It does nothing when request metrics are off, so the same front controller works with or without a store.

To count CSP violations in raw PHP, call `helmet_metrics_requests($config)?->cspViolation($directive)` from the handler that receives your reports.

#### Check it[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/metrics.html#check-it)

```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $HELMET_METRICS_TOKEN" https://your-app.example.test/metrics | head
```

Expect `helmet_info` first. Without the token you should get `403`; with metrics off, `404`.

### Graph it in Grafana[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/metrics.html#graph-it-in-grafana)

The fleet dashboard ships in [`docs/grafana/helmet.json`](https://git.wayne.edu/enterprise-apps/helmet/-/blob/main/docs/grafana/helmet.json). In Grafana, open Dashboards, New, Import, upload the file, and pick your Prometheus data source for the `DS_PROMETHEUS` input. It has three rows:

- **Fleet**: apps reporting, targets down, PHP support status, days to PHP end of support, the HELMET and PHP versions in use, and the stack packages each app runs.
- **Requests**: request rate by route group and by status class, p50 and p95 latency, p95 per route group, the share of 5xx answers, store health, and CSP violations by directive. Empty until an app sets a store.
- **Scrape**: whether Prometheus reached each target over time, and every reporting instance with its versions.

`job` and `instance` variables at the top narrow every panel. The dashboard was checked against a local Prometheus and Grafana with three apps on APCu, SQLite and Redis, in light and dark themes.

A scrape config for one app, with the token kept in a file:

```yaml
scrape_configs:
  - job_name: helmet
    metrics_path: /metrics
    scheme: https
    authorization:
      credentials_file: /etc/prometheus/secrets/helmet-token
    static_configs:
      - targets:
          - your-app.example.test
```

Queries worth keeping:

```promql
# Days until each app's PHP release loses security support
min by (instance) ((helmet_php_eol_timestamp_seconds - time()) / 86400)

# Requests per second by route group (the histogram's _count is the request count)
sum by (route) (rate(helmet_http_request_duration_seconds_count[5m]))

# p95 latency
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(helmet_http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])))
```

WSU has no Prometheus server yet (decision D-024), so the dashboard is ready, not live: it graphs as soon as a server exists and scrapes `/metrics`. The stack's own sites turn it on first.

### Limits[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/metrics.html#limits)

- HELMET reports; it does not alert. Alert rules belong with the Prometheus server.
- Request metrics start at the front controller. A static file the web server answers on its own is never counted.
- The status gauge says `unknown` when no policy is set or the policy has no entry for the running PHP release.

The endpoint is the only place in HELMET that says "I am still here" without saying "here is your page". A lullaby, in a way. A helmet with a heart-rate monitor, if you like.

### Related[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/metrics.html#related)

- [Customizing the CSP](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/csp.html)
- [Platform presets](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/platform-presets.html)
- [Environment variables](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html)
- [The session](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/session.html)
