Source: https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/platform-presets.html

## Platform presets[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/platform-presets.html#platform-presets)

A preset names a platform's trusted-proxy list, so an app does not hard-code an address that belongs to the platform, not the app. Name a preset (or list your own proxies) and the same package runs on Citadel, plain Docker, OpenShift or Coolify without a code change; when you are done choosing a preset, see [Running off Citadel](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/running-off-citadel.html) for the per-platform table.

### The presets[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/platform-presets.html#the-presets)

The presets live in `Waynestate\Helmet\Platform\Presets`:

| Preset | Trusted proxies |
| --- | --- |
| `citadel` | the Docker bridge gateway to the HA-Proxy front (see [Running off Citadel](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/running-off-citadel.html)) |
| `docker` | none: a plain Docker network with no front proxy |

`citadel` is the WSU container platform: the app container talks to the HA-Proxy front through the Docker bridge gateway `172.18.0.1`, the only address allowed to set `X-Forwarded-Proto`. `docker` is a plain Docker deployment with no front proxy in front of the app container: nothing is trusted, and HTTPS is detected from the direct connection only.

### Passing a preset[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/platform-presets.html#passing-a-preset)

Raw PHP passes the preset name:

```php
$helmet = helmet_boot([
    'preset' => 'citadel',
]);
```

Laravel reads it from `HELMET_PRESET` (Playbook supplies it when the environment has none); an explicit `HELMET_PROXIES` always wins over the preset.

Off the WSU platform, skip the preset and pass your own list of the addresses your front proxy connects from:

```php
$helmet = helmet_boot([
    'trusted_proxies' => ['203.0.113.10'],
]);
```

An unknown preset name throws at boot, so a typo fails loudly instead of silently trusting nothing.

Note

With neither a preset nor a list, no address is trusted, so forwarded headers such as `X-Forwarded-Proto` are ignored and the request is read as it arrived.

### The API[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/platform-presets.html#the-api)

`Presets` exposes three static methods:

| Method | What it returns |
| --- | --- |
| `Presets::proxies(string $name)` | The trusted proxies for a preset, as a list of addresses. Throws `UnknownPresetException` if the preset is not known. |
| `Presets::exists(string $name)` | Whether a preset is known. |
| `Presets::names()` | The known preset names. |

### Which headers a trusted proxy may set[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/platform-presets.html#which-headers-a-trusted-proxy-may-set)

The headers a trusted front proxy may set are the same for every preset: `X-Forwarded-For` and `X-Forwarded-Proto` (`Presets::TRUSTED_HEADERS`). Two more are deliberately left out:

- `X-Forwarded-Host` and `X-Forwarded-Prefix`: a platform that rewrites the host (for example OpenShift, which appends the route host) would let a client pre-seed those headers.
- `X-Forwarded-Port`: Citadel's HA-Proxy never sends it, so a client-sent value would pass through untouched and change the port the app reports.

### Related[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/platform-presets.html#related)

- [WSU values (Playbook)](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/wsu-values.html)
- [Running off Citadel](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/running-off-citadel.html)
- [HTTPS, and why the proxy list matters](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/https-and-proxies.html)
- [Environment variables](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html)

Source: https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html

## Quick start[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html#quick-start)

This is the raw PHP path, the shortest one. Laravel and PSR-15 mount the same core as middleware; see the [Next steps](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html#next-steps) section at the bottom.

1. **Add the package.**
   ```
   composer require waynestate/helmet
   ```
   Expected: Composer adds `waynestate/helmet` to `composer.json` and installs it with its dependencies.
2. **Boot it once**, at the top of the front controller, before anything is echoed:
   ```php
   use function Waynestate\Helmet\helmet_boot;
   
   $helmet = helmet_boot([
       'preset' => 'citadel',
   ]);
   ```
   Expected: `helmet_boot()` sends the headers, strips `X-Powered-By`, and answers `/up` with `200 ok` before your code runs. It returns the nonce, the logger and the request ID.
3. **Ask the load balancer's question.**
   ```
   curl -sI http://localhost/up
   ```
   Expected: `200 ok`, with the baseline headers on the response and no `X-Powered-By`.
4. **Put the nonce in your scripts.** `$helmet['nonce']` is the per-request CSP nonce: print the meta tag in `<head>` and put the nonce in your `<script>` tags.
   ```php
   echo helmet_csp_nonce_meta($helmet['nonce']);
   ```
   Expected: inline scripts tagged with the nonce pass the CSP, because `script-src` carries the nonce plus `strict-dynamic`.

### What you built[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html#what-you-built)

A raw PHP front controller where every response carries the baseline security headers, `X-Powered-By` is stripped, `/up` answers the load balancer before your code runs, and inline scripts carry the per-request CSP nonce. One call, and the floor is set.

### Next steps[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html#next-steps)

- Go deeper by stack: [Raw PHP](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-raw-php.html), [PSR-15 middleware](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-psr15.html), [Laravel](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-laravel.html).
- What goes on the wire: [The headers](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/headers.html).
- Platform presets and proxies: [Platform presets](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/platform-presets.html), [HTTPS, and why the proxy list matters](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/https-and-proxies.html).
- Every knob: [Environment variables](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html).

---

Source: https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/running-off-citadel.html

## Running off Citadel[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/running-off-citadel.html#running-off-citadel)

HELMET ships one package for every platform, so running off Citadel means changing configuration, not code. Pick the row for your platform below, set `HELMET_PROXIES` or a preset, and point logs at `php://stderr`; for what a preset is, see [Platform presets](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/platform-presets.html).

### The platforms[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/running-off-citadel.html#the-platforms)

The only platform fact HELMET needs is the address of whatever stands in front of the app container:

| Platform | What sits in front | `HELMET_PROXIES` | Where logs go |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Citadel | HA-Proxy | use the `citadel` preset (`172.18.0.1`) | `/var/log/app/helmet.log`, the preset's file path |
| OpenShift | the OpenShift router | the router's pod network CIDR, from your cluster admin | `php://stderr` |
| Coolify | Traefik or Caddy | the Docker network of the proxy | `php://stderr` |
| Raw Docker behind a compose proxy | your proxy service | the compose network's subnet | `php://stderr` |

### The citadel caveat[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/running-off-citadel.html#the-citadel-caveat)

One caveat about the `citadel` row: `172.18.0.1` is the Docker bridge gateway, and the `citadel` preset is safe only when the front proxy reaches the app over that bridge. A published app port that is source-NATed to the gateway address would make a direct client look like the proxy, so the platform must not publish the app's port.

Warning

If the platform publishes the app's port, a direct client can appear to come from the gateway address and set `X-Forwarded-Proto`. Keep the app's port unpublished while you use the `citadel` preset.

### Overrides and the no-trust default[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/running-off-citadel.html#overrides-and-the-no-trust-default)

An explicit `HELMET_PROXIES` overrides the preset on every platform. With neither a preset nor a list, no address is trusted, so forwarded headers such as `X-Forwarded-Proto` are ignored and the request is read as it arrived. Off Citadel, log to `php://stderr` and let the container runtime collect the lines.

The helmet comes off the platform, not the app.

### Related[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/running-off-citadel.html#related)

- [Platform presets](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/platform-presets.html)
- [WSU values (Playbook)](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/wsu-values.html)
- [HTTPS, and why the proxy list matters](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/https-and-proxies.html)
- [Environment variables](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html)

Source: https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/session.html

## The session[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/session.html#the-session)

This page covers the session hardening HELMET applies before the first `session_start()`: the `ini` values it sets, the cookie name rule, and how Secure mode works. Read it before you deploy a raw PHP app, then move on to [The request-forgery guard](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/csrf.html) for the next layer.

A session is the one thing you want nobody to forge, steal, or pin down early. HELMET tightens the screws before the first `session_start()`, so the cookie is as hard to misuse as the headers are to spoof.

### The goal[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/session.html#the-goal)

Call `SessionHardening::apply()` once, before the session starts, and let it set the session `ini` values that the platform's shared `php.ini` leaves at insecure defaults. It refuses to run once a session is active, because changing them mid-session does nothing. In raw PHP the call happens inside `helmet_boot()`; in Laravel the adapter does not apply it, so the framework's own session config applies instead.

### The settings[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/session.html#the-settings)

`SessionHardening::apply()` sets these `ini` values before the session starts:

| Setting | Value | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `session.use_strict_mode` | `1` | Rejects session IDs the server did not issue, which blocks fixation. |
| `session.use_only_cookies` | `1` | The session ID travels only in the cookie, never in a URL. |
| `session.cookie_httponly` | `1` | JavaScript cannot read the session cookie. |
| `session.cookie_samesite` | `Lax` | Cuts cross-site session reuse. |
| `session.cookie_secure` | `1` on HTTPS, or always in `always` mode, unset otherwise | The cookie is sent only over TLS, and plain-HTTP setups keep working. |
| `session.cookie_lifetime` | `0` | A browser-session cookie: it ends when the browser closes. |
| `session.cache_limiter` | `nocache` | Pages cannot be cached and replayed with the session attached. |
| `session.cookie_path` | `/` | The usual scope, and required by the `__Host-` prefix. |
| `session.cookie_domain` | empty | Host-only: the cookie is not sent to sibling subdomains. |
| `session.name` | `__Host-WSUSESSID` on HTTPS, `WSUSESSID` on HTTP | A generic name reveals less, and the `__Host-` prefix makes the browser reject the cookie unless it is `Secure`, `Path=/` and has no `Domain`. |

Note

`session.sid_length` is deliberately not touched. It is deprecated as of PHP 8.4 and the platform image sets it to 26, so changing it here would fight the platform. That change is left to the Upgrade project.

### The cookie name rule[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/session.html#the-cookie-name-rule)

The name rule applies only while the name is still PHP's default `PHPSESSID`. An app that chose its own name keeps it, and SESAME reads whatever `session_name()` returns, so a changed name is safe for it. When an app first runs this version, existing sessions under the old name end: the next request still carries the old cookie, the app finds no session under the new name and starts a fresh one.

Warning

Deploying this version ends every session that still uses the default `PHPSESSID` name. Signed-in users sign in once more after the deploy.

### Secure mode[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/session.html#secure-mode)

By default (`auto`) the Secure flag follows the request. On Citadel, HA-Proxy ends TLS before the request reaches PHP, so the request looks plain even though the client connected over HTTPS; there, set `HELMET_SESSION_SECURE=always` so the cookie keeps its `Secure` flag. In Laravel the value lands in `helmet.session.secure`; in raw PHP pass `'session' => ['secure' => 'always']` to `helmet_boot()`, and a Laravel app that boots through `helmet_boot()` can hand it `config('helmet.session.secure')`.

The cookie name still follows the request, so it never takes the `__Host-` prefix on a plain-HTTP request, and plain HTTP development keeps `auto`.

Note

For session hardening in Laravel, use the framework's own session config: set `secure`, `http_only`, and `same_site` in `config/session.php` rather than expecting the adapter to apply raw-PHP `SessionHardening`.

### Failure behavior[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/session.html#failure-behavior)

`apply()` throws a `LogicException` if a session is already active, and a `RuntimeException` naming the first setting that could not be changed if any `ini` value refuses to be set. A setting that cannot be changed is a loud failure, not a silent insecure default.

### Related[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/session.html#related)

- [The request-forgery guard](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/csrf.html)
- [Metrics](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/metrics.html)

---

Source: https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-laravel.html

## Laravel[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-laravel.html#laravel)

This page walks the Laravel adapter from `composer require` to a fully wired app: install the adapter, publish the config, trust the proxy, then turn the knobs. The adapter is a service provider, two always-on middlewares, an optional request-forgery guard, and a config file. It only wires and configures: every rule (what the headers say, how a nonce is made, how a CSP is merged, and how a request-forgery check is applied) lives in the core, so Laravel and raw PHP cannot drift apart. The suite runs against Laravel 13 with Orchestra Testbench. Helmet is the band, and the name fits: put it on before you ship.

### Install the adapter[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-laravel.html#install-the-adapter)

Strap It On:

```bash
composer require waynestate/helmet
```

Package discovery registers `Waynestate\Helmet\Laravel\HelmetServiceProvider`, so there is nothing to add to `bootstrap/providers.php`. The provider merges the `helmet` config and joins the HTTP kernel's middleware:

- `SecurityHeaders` sends the headers in [The headers](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/headers.html) and strips `X-Powered-By`. By default it is global, so 404s and JSON routes carry them too.
- `InjectRibbon` adds the environment ribbon ([The ribbon](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-laravel.html#the-ribbon)). It always stays in the `web` group, because it edits HTML.
- `RequestForgeryGuard` is opt-in. When `helmet.csrf.enabled` is true, it joins the `web` group after `InjectRibbon` and applies the check in [The request-forgery guard](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/csrf.html).

They are added through the HTTP kernel, so they survive another package adding to the same group. Set `HELMET_SCOPE=web` to keep `SecurityHeaders` in the `web` group only; then routes outside `web` and unmatched 404s do not carry its headers.

At boot the provider also registers two route macros: `Route::cspReport()` for the CSP report endpoint ([Customizing the CSP](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/csp.html)) and `Route::helmetMetrics()` for the metrics endpoint ([Metrics](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/metrics.html)). Both macros are always registered, but each route is added only when the app calls it, so both endpoints stay off by default.

### Publish the config[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-laravel.html#publish-the-config)

```bash
php artisan vendor:publish --tag=helmet-config
```

This copies `config/helmet.php` into your app. Do it: it is the best place to change the CSP, because the policy is a PHP array there, not JSON squeezed into `.env`. The config file is also the one place HELMET reads the environment (`env()`, plus `HELMET_PRESET` through `Setting`, which also checks Playbook), so `php artisan config:cache` keeps working.

### Trust the proxy[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-laravel.html#trust-the-proxy)

HELMET decides on its own whether a request was really HTTPS, from `HELMET_PROXIES`. Laravel has a separate trusted-proxy setting that drives `url()`, secure cookies and `$request->isSecure()`. The provider follows the same list: when the app has not set `trustedproxy.proxies` itself, it copies `helmet.proxies` over, so `HELMET_PROXIES` drives both. An app that sets `trustedproxy.proxies` keeps its own value, and an explicit `trustProxies(at: ...)` call in `bootstrap/app.php` still wins, because Laravel applies it before the config fallback.

The provider also narrows which forwarded headers Laravel believes from those proxies: `X-Forwarded-For` and `X-Forwarded-Proto`, and nothing else. Laravel's own default also trusts `X-Forwarded-Host`, `X-Forwarded-Prefix` and `X-Forwarded-Port`, and a client can pre-seed any of them on a platform whose proxy does not overwrite them, which poisons `url()`, redirects and password-reset links. Port is out for the same reason: Citadel's HA-Proxy never sends it at all, so a client-sent value would pass through untouched and change the port Laravel reports and the URLs it generates. If your app needs one of them, choose the set yourself with `trustProxies(at: ..., headers: ...)` in `bootstrap/app.php` (or `TrustProxies::withHeaders()`); HELMET then leaves your choice alone.

Citadel's HA-Proxy *appends* `X-Forwarded-Proto` instead of replacing it, so a client can arrive with two values, `https, http`. Symfony reads the first value of such a list (the client's), while HELMET reads the last (the one the closest proxy appended). To keep Laravel in agreement, the provider prepends a small middleware to the global chain that rewrites the header to its last value when the request comes from a trusted proxy. A single value is left alone, and requests from untrusted peers are ignored as before.

As in the [Raw PHP](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-raw-php.html) path, use a [preset](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/platform-presets.html) or list only the address your front proxy connects from, never a whole private range. See [Running off Citadel](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/running-off-citadel.html) for the platform layout.

The `/up` health route is Laravel's own: keep `health: '/up'` in `withRouting()`. The adapter registers no route. Keep `/up` for liveness only: readiness checks (database, cache) belong on a separate `/ready` route, as described in [Readiness is a separate check](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-raw-php.html#readiness-is-a-separate-check); do not put them in the `DiagnosingHealth` listener, which fires for `/up`.

### Environment variables[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-laravel.html#environment-variables)

| Variable | Config key | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `HELMET_SCOPE` | `helmet.scope` | `global` | `global` puts `SecurityHeaders` in the kernel's global middleware; `web` keeps it in the `web` group only. `InjectRibbon` always stays in `web`. |
| `HELMET_PRESET` | `helmet.preset` | none | A platform preset name (`citadel` or `docker`) that supplies the trusted proxies. Read from the environment, else from Playbook (see [WSU values (Playbook)](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/wsu-values.html)). `HELMET_PROXIES` wins when both are set. An unknown name throws, even when `HELMET_PROXIES` is set. |
| `HELMET_PROXIES` | `helmet.proxies` | none | Comma-separated IPs or CIDR ranges allowed to set `X-Forwarded-Proto`. Wins over `HELMET_PRESET`. Also copied to `trustedproxy.proxies` when the app has not set it. An explicitly empty value (`HELMET_PROXIES=`) trusts nobody, even when `HELMET_PRESET` is set; only an unset variable falls back to the preset. |
| `HELMET_CSP` | `helmet.csp` | the core default policy | A JSON policy array, merged over the default (see below). Empty or invalid JSON keeps the default. |
| `HELMET_HSTS_MAX_AGE` | `helmet.hsts` | `31536000` | The HSTS `max-age` in seconds, sent on HTTPS only. It must not be negative. |
| `HELMET_HSTS_INCLUDE_SUBDOMAINS` | `helmet.hsts_include_subdomains` | `true` | Set `false` to omit the HSTS `includeSubDomains` directive. |
| `HELMET_HSTS_PRELOAD` | `helmet.hsts_preload` | `false` | Set `true` to append the `preload` directive to HSTS. Requires `max-age` of at least one year and `includeSubDomains`. |
| `HELMET_CSP_TRUSTED_TYPES_ENABLED` | `helmet.csp_trusted_types.enabled` | `false` | Set `true` to append Trusted Types directives to the report-only CSP header. |
| `HELMET_CSP_TRUSTED_TYPES_POLICIES` | `helmet.csp_trusted_types.policies` | `["default"]` | Comma-separated Trusted Types policy names. |
| `HELMET_NO_STORE_ENABLED` | `helmet.no_store.enabled` | `false` | Set `true` to send `Cache-Control: no-store` on matching responses. |
| `HELMET_NO_STORE_PATHS` | `helmet.no_store.paths` | none | Comma-separated path prefixes that carry no-store. Empty means every response. |
| `HELMET_RIBBON` | `helmet.ribbon` | `true` | Set `false` to switch the ribbon off everywhere. |
| `HELMET_POLICY_PATH` | `helmet.policy_path` | none | Path to a CREED `policy.json`. When set, the ribbon shows a version warning for the running PHP (and, in Laravel, the framework) version. A missing or invalid file shows no warning and never breaks the page. |
| `HELMET_DEV_ORIGIN` | `helmet.dev_origin` | none | The Vite dev server origin, used in `local` only when the dev server is running. Must be `http` or `https` on `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` or `[::1]`. Overrides the hot file. |
| `HELMET_CSP_REPORT_URI` | `helmet.csp_report_uri` | none | The URL browsers POST CSP violation reports to. Adds `report-uri` and `report-to` to the policy and a `Reporting-Endpoints` header. Must be `https`. |
| `HELMET_CSP_REPORT_ONLY` | `helmet.csp_report_only` | `false` | Set `true` to send the policy as `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only` (observe violations without blocking them). |
| `HELMET_CSRF_ENABLED` | `helmet.csrf.enabled` | `false` | Set `true` to turn on the request-forgery guard for state-changing requests. |
| `HELMET_CSRF_ALLOW_SAME_SITE` | `helmet.csrf.allow_same_site` | `false` | Set `true` to let `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-site` pass. Off by default because sibling subdomains are still same-site. |
| `HELMET_CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS` | `helmet.csrf.trusted_origins` | none | Comma-separated origins allowed to make state-changing requests when the `Origin` fallback is used. |
| `HELMET_CSRF_EXCEPT` | `helmet.csrf.except` | none | Comma-separated path patterns that skip the guard: an exact path, a prefix ending in `*`, or `*` for every path. |
| `HELMET_WARN_DEBUG` | `helmet.warn_debug` | `true` | Set `false` to stop the one boot-time warning the adapter logs when the app boots with `app.debug` true in `production`. |

Warning

Preload is hard to undo: once a browser has preloaded the domain it refuses plain-HTTP connections until the entry is removed.

### Customizing the CSP in Laravel[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-laravel.html#customizing-the-csp-in-laravel)

`helmet.csp` takes the same shape as the raw PHP `csp` option and follows the same rule: it is merged over the default, per directive. A directive you set replaces the default's, a directive you leave out keeps it, and `null` removes one. Open the published `config/helmet.php` and replace the `$csp = SecurityHeaders::defaultCspPolicy();` line:

```php
$csp = [
    'img-src' => ["'self'", 'data:', 'https://images.example.edu'],
    'form-action' => null,
];
```

If you would rather use the environment, `HELMET_CSP` takes the same array as JSON. In a `.env` file it needs double quotes and escaped inner quotes, which is the reason to publish the config instead:

```ini
HELMET_CSP="{\"img-src\":[\"'self'\",\"data:\"],\"form-action\":null}"
```

Invalid JSON is ignored and the default policy stays, so a typo in the environment cannot loosen the CSP. For the merge rule and report-only mode, see [Customizing the CSP](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/csp.html).

Warning

One gotcha when overriding: the policy adds the per-request nonce to `style-src` and `style-src-elem`. A browser ignores `'unsafe-inline'` once a nonce is present, so setting `style-src` to `["'unsafe-inline'"]` does not restore inline styles; it removes them.

### The nonce in Blade[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-laravel.html#the-nonce-in-blade)

The middleware puts the per-request nonce on the request as the attribute `helmet.csp_nonce`, the same name the PSR-15 middleware uses. It also hands the nonce to Laravel's Vite helper, so `@vite` needs nothing: the `script` and `style` tags it print already carry the nonce the CSP header sends.

For an inline script, print the nonce from the Vite helper:

```blade
<script nonce="{{ Vite::cspNonce() }}">
    // allowed by the nonce, and free to load more scripts (strict-dynamic)
</script>
```

In a controller it is `$request->attributes->get('helmet.csp_nonce')`. A new nonce is made for every request. Repetition is a fine Helmet song and a terrible nonce.

### Vite and Inertia[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-laravel.html#vite-and-inertia)

The middleware hands the per-request nonce to Laravel's Vite helper and injects a `csp-nonce` meta tag into `<head>`. `@vite` needs nothing. The meta tag lets Vite's dev runtime nonce the CSS and preload tags it adds after page load. When the request ends, HELMET resets the Vite nonce to a fresh random one, so a long-lived worker (Octane, Swoole, FrankenPHP) does not carry one request's nonce into the next.

A few rules keep the CSP honest:

- **Nonce every inline script.** The CSP has no `'unsafe-inline'` for scripts. Every `<script>` without a `src` needs `nonce="{{ Vite::cspNonce() }}"`.
- **No `'unsafe-eval'`.** The CSP never allows it. If your bundle needs `eval`, fix the bundle.
- **No scripts in Inertia's `<Head>`.** Inertia's `<Head>` renders into the document head after the page loads. A `<script>` there would not carry the nonce, and the browser would block it. Put scripts in your layout, where `@vite` and the nonce reach them.
- **No second nonce-producing package.** If another package calls `Vite::useCspNonce()` after HELMET, the `@vite` tags carry a different nonce than the CSP header, and the browser blocks the scripts. The middleware logs a warning when it detects this.
- **No shared caching of nonced HTML.** The nonce changes every request. A cached page would carry a stale nonce, and the browser would block its scripts. Do not cache HTML at a layer that shares it across requests.
- **Do not replace `style-src` with `'unsafe-inline'`.** The policy adds the per-request nonce to `style-src` and `style-src-elem`, and a browser ignores `'unsafe-inline'` once a nonce is present. An override that relies on it loses every inline style silently. Keep the nonce, move the styles into files, or give the inline styles a nonce.

In raw PHP, print the meta tag in `<head>` with the nonce `helmet_boot()` returned:

```php
echo helmet_csp_nonce_meta($helmet['nonce']);
```

The Vite dev server is allowed in the `local` environment only, and only when it is running (a hot file exists). The origin comes from `HELMET_DEV_ORIGIN` when set, otherwise from the hot file. It must be `http` or `https` on `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` or `[::1]`, with an optional port. An invalid origin is ignored and a warning is logged. In every other environment the dev server origin is never added.

### The ribbon[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-laravel.html#the-ribbon)

In `local`, `development`, `dev`, `testing`, `test` and `staging`, `InjectRibbon` adds `<div class="helmet-ribbon" data-environment="staging">staging</div>` right after the opening `<body>` tag of an HTML response, so nobody mistakes a test site for the real one. It never appears in `production`, on JSON or other non-HTML responses, or on HTML with no `<body>`. The package ships no stylesheet; style `.helmet-ribbon` in your own CSS. Even with `HELMET_RIBBON=true`, production never gets it, so there is no Aftertaste.

**Version warnings.** Point `HELMET_POLICY_PATH` at a CREED `policy.json` and the ribbon gains a warning line for each component version that is in its security-only phase or end of life. The raw PHP path checks the running PHP version; the Laravel adapter also checks the framework's major version. With no policy path there is no warning and no file read, and a missing, unreadable or invalid file shows no warning and never breaks the page. Style `.helmet-ribbon-warning` in your own CSS.

### Raw PHP and Laravel agree[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-laravel.html#raw-php-and-laravel-agree)

Both paths call `SecurityHeaders::build()`, so for the same request and settings they send the same headers. A test pins that down: it compares what the Laravel middleware sends, name and value, with `build()`. The settings map like this:

| Setting | Raw PHP (`helmet_boot()`) | Laravel |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Trusted proxies | `trusted_proxies` | `HELMET_PROXIES` / `helmet.proxies` |
| CSP overrides | `csp` | `HELMET_CSP` / `helmet.csp`, same merge, `null` removes |
| HSTS max-age | `hsts_max_age` | `HELMET_HSTS_MAX_AGE` / `helmet.hsts` |
| HSTS subdomains | `hsts_include_subdomains` | `HELMET_HSTS_INCLUDE_SUBDOMAINS` / `helmet.hsts_include_subdomains`, default `true` |
| HSTS preload | `hsts_preload` | `HELMET_HSTS_PRELOAD` / `helmet.hsts_preload`, default `false` |
| Trusted Types | `csp_trusted_types` | `HELMET_CSP_TRUSTED_TYPES_*` / `helmet.csp_trusted_types.*`, default off |
| no-store | `no_store` | `HELMET_NO_STORE_*` / `helmet.no_store.*`, default off |
| CSP report URI | `csp_report_uri` | `HELMET_CSP_REPORT_URI` / `helmet.csp_report_uri` |
| CSP report-only | `csp_report_only` | `HELMET_CSP_REPORT_ONLY` / `helmet.csp_report_only`, default `false` |
| COOP | `coop` | `HELMET_COOP` / `helmet.coop`, default `same-origin`, `null` sends no header |
| CORP | `corp` | `HELMET_CORP` / `helmet.corp`, default `null` (no header) |
| Permissions-Policy | `permissions_policy` | `HELMET_PERMISSIONS_POLICY` / `helmet.permissions_policy`, default deny list, `[]` sends no header |
| Nonce | `$helmet['nonce']` | `request()->attributes->get('helmet.csp_nonce')` |
| Health check | `health_path`, answered by `helmet_boot()` | Laravel's `health: '/up'` |
| Request-forgery guard | `csrf` option to `helmet_boot()` | `helmet.csrf.*` / `HELMET_CSRF_*`; the middleware is registered only when enabled |
| Session hardening, JSON logs | applied by `helmet_boot()` | not applied by the adapter; Laravel's session and logging config apply |

For session hardening in Laravel, use the framework's own session config: set `secure`, `http_only`, and `same_site` in `config/session.php` rather than expecting the adapter to apply raw-PHP `SessionHardening`. For structured logs, use Laravel's log channels, for example the `stderr` channel, rather than expecting the adapter to configure a raw-PHP logger. The first two security events ([Security events](https://github.com/waynestate/helmet#security-events)) are written through the Log facade with the same message and context, and the third, `helmet.debug_enabled_in_production`, is written by the Laravel adapter at boot. The check runs at boot, not per request: the value is fixed for the life of the process, and a long-lived worker must not log it on every request. Both sides are checked strictly: `app.debug` must be the boolean `true`, and the environment must be exactly `production`. Opt out with `helmet.warn_debug` (env `HELMET_WARN_DEBUG`); a logging failure is swallowed and never breaks the boot.

- [Configuring HSTS](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/hsts.html)

## Use HELMET as PSR-15 middleware[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-psr15.html#use-helmet-as-psr-15-middleware)

This page mounts the same HELMET core in a PSR-15 middleware pipeline. Copy the pipeline in [Mount the pipeline](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-psr15.html#mount-the-pipeline), then decide which middlewares your app needs and how errors should flow.

### Mount the pipeline[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-psr15.html#mount-the-pipeline)

The same core, mounted in a middleware pipeline:

```php
use Nyholm\Psr7\Factory\Psr17Factory;
use Waynestate\Helmet\Csrf\RequestForgeryGuard;
use Waynestate\Helmet\Headers\SecurityHeadersMiddleware;
use Waynestate\Helmet\Health\HealthCheck;
use Waynestate\Helmet\Platform\Presets;
use Waynestate\Helmet\Proxy\TrustedProxies;

$factory = new Psr17Factory();
$proxies = new TrustedProxies(Presets::proxies('citadel'));

$middleware = [
    new HealthCheck($factory, $factory, '/up'),
    new RequestForgeryGuard($proxies, $factory, $factory, except: ['/api/webhooks/*']),
    new SecurityHeadersMiddleware($proxies),
];
```

### The middlewares[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-psr15.html#the-middlewares)

- `HealthCheck` answers the health path, `/up` in the example.
- `RequestForgeryGuard` is opt-in: mounting it turns the check on for that pipeline. The example passes `except: ['/api/webhooks/*']`. Its options are described in [The request-forgery guard](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/csrf.html).
- `SecurityHeadersMiddleware` sets the request attribute `helmet.csp_nonce` so a downstream handler can read the same nonce the CSP header carries.

On every request, `SecurityHeadersMiddleware`:

- decides whether the request is HTTPS from the trusted-proxy list,
- builds the headers, including a per-request CSP nonce,
- exposes the nonce to the application as the `helmet.csp_nonce` request attribute,
- removes the `X-Powered-By` header.

The headers are sent even when the inner handler throws. When no-store is enabled and the request path matches (`noStorePaths` is empty for every response) and the response carries no `Cache-Control` header, the middleware adds `Cache-Control: no-store`.

### Errors and rethrow[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-psr15.html#errors-and-rethrow)

By default the middleware rethrows, so the framework's error handler still runs and produces the error page, and the middleware attaches the headers only to responses that come back through it; pass `rethrow: false` (and a PSR-17 `ResponseFactory`) to make the middleware itself return a `500` carrying the same headers. The raw PHP path needs no such flag: `helmet_boot()` sends the headers before your code runs, so they are already on the wire by the time an exception can happen.

The `500` response carries `Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8`. If `rethrow` is false and no `ResponseFactory` was passed, the middleware throws a `\RuntimeException` when it needs to build the `500`.

### Put HELMET outermost[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-psr15.html#put-helmet-outermost)

Order decides whether an error page gets the headers. A response built by a layer inside HELMET comes back through HELMET and is stamped; a response built by a layer outside HELMET never is. So HELMET has to be the outermost layer. In a Slim-style app, where the middleware added last runs first, that means adding HELMET after the error middleware. If the error middleware sits outside HELMET, the exception passes straight through (HELMET rethrows by default) and the error middleware builds a bare `500` with no security headers. `tests/Headers/SecurityHeadersMiddlewareTest.php` pins both orders with a stand-in error middleware.

### Constructor options[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-psr15.html#constructor-options)

| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `proxies` | required | the `TrustedProxies` list used to decide whether the request is HTTPS |
| `cspPolicy` | `null` | merged per directive over the default policy; a directive set to `null` is removed; `null` uses the default policy unchanged |
| `rethrow` | `true` | rethrow when the inner handler throws so the framework's error handler runs; when `false`, return a `500` with the security headers instead |
| `responseFactory` | `null` | builds the `500` response when `rethrow` is false; only needed on that path |
| `hstsMaxAge` | `31536000` | the HSTS max-age in seconds, sent only on HTTPS |
| `hstsIncludeSubDomains` | `true` | whether HSTS covers subdomains, sent only on HTTPS |
| `cspReportUri` | `null` | the CSP report destination, or `null` to send no reporting directives |
| `cspReportOnly` | `false` | when true, the policy is sent as `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only` instead of `Content-Security-Policy` |
| `coop` | `'same-origin'` | the Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy value, or `null` to send no COOP header |
| `corp` | `null` | the Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy value, or `null` to send no CORP header |
| `permissionsPolicy` | `null` | the Permissions-Policy feature map, or `null` to use the default deny list; an empty array sends no Permissions-Policy header |
| `hstsPreload` | `false` | whether to append the preload directive to HSTS, sent only on HTTPS |
| `trustedTypesEnabled` | `false` | whether to append the Trusted Types directives to the report-only CSP header |
| `trustedTypesPolicies` | `['default']` | the Trusted Types policy names, used when `trustedTypesEnabled` is true |
| `noStoreEnabled` | `false` | whether to send `Cache-Control: no-store` on matching responses |
| `noStorePaths` | `[]` | path prefixes that carry no-store, or empty for every response |

Note

The cross-origin isolation settings are validated at construction, not per request: a bad `coop`, `corp`, `permissionsPolicy` or `trustedTypesPolicies` value is a config error, and it fails where the app starts, not on the first request, with an `\InvalidArgumentException`.

- [Raw PHP](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-raw-php.html)
- [Laravel](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-laravel.html)

## Use HELMET in raw PHP[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-raw-php.html#use-helmet-in-raw-php)

This page boots HELMET in a framework-free PHP app with a single call. Start with [Boot the app](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-raw-php.html#boot-the-app), then pick up the options your app needs: structured logs, the request-forgery guard, the opt-in error handler, and the standalone health check.

### Boot the app[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-raw-php.html#boot-the-app)

At the top of the front controller, before anything is echoed:

```php
use function Waynestate\Helmet\helmet_boot;

$helmet = helmet_boot([
    // The platform preset that supplies the trusted proxies. An explicit
    // 'trusted_proxies' list wins over the preset.
    'preset' => 'citadel',

    // Optional. A Monolog JSON logger, one line per record. "stream" may be a
    // stream or a file path. Off Citadel, lead with php://stderr; the
    // Citadel preset's value is /var/log/app/helmet.log. Every record carries
    // a request ID in extra.request_id, generated by HELMET; an inbound
    // header is never trusted for it. Set "request_id" to reuse an ID you
    // already have (8 to 64 letters, digits, dots, underscores or dashes).
    'log' => [
        'channel' => 'app',
        'stream'  => 'php://stderr',
        'level'   => 'info',
        // 'request_id' => 'req-20261029-abcd',
    ],
]);

// $helmet['nonce'] is the per-request CSP nonce. Put it in your <script> tags.
// $helmet['logger'] is a Psr\Log\LoggerInterface, or null when no log is set.
// $helmet['request_id'] is the ID stamped on this process's log records.
```

`helmet_boot()` sends the headers, strips `X-Powered-By`, and answers `/up` with `200 ok` before your code runs. It returns the nonce, the logger and the request ID so the rest of the app can use them.

It reads `$_SERVER` directly rather than building a PSR-7 request, so it works in plain PHP without a server-request factory. In order, it:

- decides whether the request is HTTPS from the trusted-proxy list,
- hardens the session settings (throws if a session is already active),
- removes the `X-Powered-By` header,
- answers the health check path with `ok` and stops,
- rejects a state-changing request when the request-forgery guard is enabled and the request is not same-origin (or from a trusted origin),
- sends the security headers (including a per-request CSP nonce),
- sets up a JSON logger (if configured).

Note

A bad config throws at boot: `UnknownPresetException` if `"preset"` names a preset the package does not know, `\InvalidArgumentException` for a wrong type or an invalid value, `InvalidCspReportUriException` if `"csp_report_uri"` is not a valid report destination, and `\LogicException` if a session is already active.

### Structured logs[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-raw-php.html#structured-logs)

Each record is one JSON line:

```json
{"message":"login","context":{"user":"alice"},"level":200,"level_name":"INFO","channel":"app","datetime":"2026-10-29T12:00:00.000000+00:00","extra":{"request_id":"9f2c1ab04d5e6f70"}}
```

When you set `log`, the channel defaults to `helmet`, the stream to `php://stderr`, and the level to `info`. The request ID rules sit in the boot snippet above: every record carries one in `extra.request_id`, generated by HELMET, and an inbound header is never trusted for it.

### Security events[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-raw-php.html#security-events)

Three warnings carry HELMET's security events, and a logger that throws never changes the answer: the `403` still goes out, the resolved client IP is still the peer, and the boot still finishes.

| Message | When | Context keys |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `helmet.request_refused` | the request-forgery guard answers `403` | `event` (`request_refused`), `method` (upper case), `path` (no query string), `sec_fetch_site` (`same-origin`, `same-site`, `cross-site`, `none`, `other`, or null when the header is absent), `origin_present` (bool) |
| `helmet.forwarded_for_rejected` | `ClientIp::resolve()` fails closed on an unparseable `X-Forwarded-For` entry | `event` (`forwarded_for_rejected`), `reason` (`unparseable_entry`), `peer` (the trusted peer address) |
| `helmet.debug_enabled_in_production` | the Laravel adapter boots with `app.debug` true in the production environment | `event` (`debug_enabled_in_production`) |

Never logged: the Origin value, cookies, Authorization, the `X-Forwarded-For` header, or the bad entry. The helmet takes the hit and reports it, without quoting the attacker.

The logger reaches each path this way: `helmet_boot()` hands its own logger to the guard; PSR-15 users pass a `LoggerInterface` as the last constructor argument `$logger` of `RequestForgeryGuard`; `helmet_metrics()` passes its configured logger to `ClientIp::resolve()`.

### Trusted proxies[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-raw-php.html#trusted-proxies)

Use a platform preset (for example `citadel`, which trusts the Docker bridge gateway), or list only the address the front proxy connects from, never a whole private range. A broad range such as `10.0.0.0/8` also trusts other containers on the same network, and any of them could then set `X-Forwarded-Proto`. An explicitly empty `HELMET_PROXIES` means trust nobody, even when a preset is set; only an unset variable falls back to the preset.

Warning

The `citadel` preset trusts the container bridge gateway address, which is only correct while the app's port is not published to the host network, because a published port can make a direct client appear to come from the gateway.

The trusted proxies come from, in order of precedence:

- `trusted_proxies`: an explicit list of IPs or CIDR ranges.
- `preset`: a platform preset name (see `Waynestate\Helmet\Platform\Presets`), for example `citadel` or `docker`.
- neither: an empty list, which trusts nothing.

### A generic error page[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-raw-php.html#a-generic-error-page)

A raw PHP app has no framework to catch an uncaught exception, so PHP may print the message, the file path and a stack trace to the visitor. Turn on the opt-in handler and the visitor gets a short, fixed "Something went wrong" page with status 500 and `Cache-Control: no-store`, while the full detail (class, message, file, line and trace) goes to the log at `error` level:

```php
helmet_boot([
    'error_handler' => ['enabled' => true],
]);
```

The page never contains anything from the exception, and a logger that throws cannot change it. It is off by default, and Laravel keeps its own exception handler. If you want to build the page yourself, call `(new \Waynestate\Helmet\Error\GenericErrorResponse())->build($exception, $logger)` for the status, headers and body as data. HELMET does not switch PHP's `display_errors` off for you; the platform setting does that.

The same class builds the 4xx half of the rule: a raw PHP app that wants a neutral 4xx page for a client fault calls `clientError()` with the status and sends the result itself:

```php
$page = (new \Waynestate\Helmet\Error\GenericErrorResponse())->clientError(404);
http_response_code($page['status']);
foreach ($page['headers'] as $name => $value) {
    header($name . ': ' . $value);
}
echo $page['body'];
```

The page is fixed text: 400, 401, 403, 404, 405, 410 and 429 each carry their own title and sentence, and any other 4xx keeps the status you passed and falls back to the Bad request text. Nothing from the request or an exception reaches the body, and a status outside the 400s throws.

### Debug output stays off in production[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-raw-php.html#debug-output-stays-off-in-production)

HELMET never switches debug output off or on for you, because the right place is the platform, not a library. Two settings decide whether a visitor can read a stack trace, and both belong to your deploy:

- **PHP's `display_errors`.** Keep it `Off` in production. Squire's deploy kit already ships a `php.ini` with `display_errors = Off` and `log_errors = On` (`deploy/.squire/php.ini` in a Squire-based app), and Citadel uses the same values. Off the platform, set it in `php.ini` or the FPM pool. HELMET does not set or check it.
- **Laravel's `APP_DEBUG`.** Keep it `false` in production. The Laravel adapter cannot stop an app from turning it on, but it notices: when the app boots with `app.debug` true in the production environment it writes one warning, `helmet.debug_enabled_in_production`, through the Log facade. Opt out with `helmet.warn_debug` (env `HELMET_WARN_DEBUG`, default `true`). A logger that fails never breaks the boot.

The opt-in error handler above covers one more case: with it on, an uncaught exception in a raw PHP app shows the fixed 500 page even if `display_errors` is wrong. Warnings and notices still follow `display_errors`, so set it anyway.

### Health check without a front controller[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-raw-php.html#health-check-without-a-front-controller)

A raw PHP app with no front controller (or an Apache setup with no rewrite) never reaches `helmet_boot()` for `/up`. Ship a two-line `public/up.php` that calls HELMET directly:

```php
<?php // public/up.php
use function Waynestate\Helmet\helmet_up;

require __DIR__ . '/../vendor/autoload.php';
helmet_up();
```

Squire's raw template ships this file. The probe only checks that the ball is in the air; it does not grade the play.

`helmet_up()` sends exactly what `helmet_boot()` sends for the health path (`200`, `Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8`, `Cache-Control: no-store`, body `ok`) and exits. No session, no other headers, no config read.

### Readiness is a separate check[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-raw-php.html#readiness-is-a-separate-check)

`/up` is liveness: "the process is running". Keep it free of dependency checks. If `/up` fails because the database is down, the platform restarts a healthy app and makes the outage worse. Put dependency checks on a different path, for example `/ready`, and point the load balancer's "send me traffic" probe at that one, not the restart probe.

```php
<?php // public/ready.php
declare(strict_types=1);

header('Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8');
header('Cache-Control: no-store');

try {
    $pdo = new PDO(getenv('DB_DSN'), getenv('DB_USER') ?: null, getenv('DB_PASSWORD') ?: null, [
        PDO::ATTR_TIMEOUT => 2,
        PDO::ATTR_ERRMODE => PDO::ERRMODE_EXCEPTION,
    ]);
    $pdo->query('SELECT 1');
    echo 'ready';
} catch (Throwable) {
    http_response_code(503);
    echo 'not ready';
}
```

Keep the same rules as `/up`: a short body, `no-store`, and no detail about which dependency failed (log that, do not print it). Give the check a short timeout so a hung database cannot hang the probe. In Laravel, register a separate `/ready` route that runs the checks; do not put them in the `DiagnosingHealth` listener, because that event fires for `/up` and would turn the liveness probe into a readiness probe.

### The nonce in your markup[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-raw-php.html#the-nonce-in-your-markup)

Tip

Vite's dev runtime reads a `<meta property="csp-nonce" nonce="...">` tag to nonce the CSS and preload tags it adds after page load. Print `helmet_csp_nonce_meta($helmet['nonce'])` in the `<head>` of every page, with the same nonce `helmet_boot()` returned. The nonce is escaped, so a nonce with a quote cannot break out of the attribute.

### Raw PHP with a Vue (Vite) build[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-raw-php.html#raw-php-with-a-vue-vite-build)

A raw PHP app that serves a built Vue/Vite SPA gives the bundler HELMET's nonce in two steps. At build time, set Vite's `html.cspNonce` to a placeholder:

```js
// vite.config.js
import { defineConfig } from 'vite';

export default defineConfig({
    html: {
        cspNonce: 'CSP_NONCE_SLOT_FOR_HELMET',
    },
});
```

On every request, replace the placeholder with the nonce `helmet_boot()` returned before you echo the page:

```php
echo helmet_csp_nonce_swap(file_get_contents('dist/index.html'), $helmet['nonce']);
```

`helmet_csp_nonce_swap()` replaces every occurrence of the placeholder with the nonce, HTML-escaped exactly the way `helmet_csp_nonce_meta()` escapes it. A placeholder shorter than 16 characters throws, so it cannot collide with page text, an empty nonce throws, and a page that carries no placeholder is returned unchanged.

One more setting keeps the CSP honest: Vite inlines small assets as `data:` URIs by default. The default policy already allows `data:` in `font-src` and `img-src`, so inlined fonts and images pass; if you would rather not inline at all, set `build.assetsInlineLimit: 0`.

## WSU values (Playbook)[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/wsu-values.html#wsu-values-playbook)

This page covers the one value HELMET reads from Playbook, `HELMET_PRESET`, and the three ways to get Playbook itself with your own GitLab token. Once the preset is set, see [Platform presets](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/platform-presets.html) for what it supplies.

### How the preset is read[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/wsu-values.html#how-the-preset-is-read)

The Laravel config reads `HELMET_PRESET` from the environment first and from the private `waynestate/playbook` package (Playbook) second, when the environment has no value. The raw PHP path takes the preset as an option to `helmet_boot()` and reads no environment at all.

| Setting | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `HELMET_PRESET` | A platform preset name (`citadel` or `docker`) that supplies the trusted proxies. |

### Get Playbook with your own GitLab token[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/wsu-values.html#get-playbook-with-your-own-gitlab-token)

Three ways.

#### Composer[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/wsu-values.html#composer)

Add the repository to your app's `composer.json`, put the token in `auth.json` (Composer's credential store, never in the repo), then require the package:

```json
{
    "repositories": [
        {
            "type": "vcs",
            "url": "https://git.wayne.edu/enterprise-apps/playbook.git"
        }
    ]
}
```

```
composer require waynestate/playbook
```

#### Fetch the values file directly[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/wsu-values.html#fetch-the-values-file-directly)

curl

```bash
curl --fail -H "PRIVATE-TOKEN: $GITLAB_TOKEN" "https://git.wayne.edu/api/v4/projects/enterprise-apps%2Fplaybook/repository/files/playbook.env/raw?ref=main" -o .env.playbook
```

powershell

```powershell
Invoke-WebRequest -Headers @{ 'PRIVATE-TOKEN' = $env:GITLAB_TOKEN } -Uri "https://git.wayne.edu/api/v4/projects/enterprise-apps%2Fplaybook/repository/files/playbook.env/raw?ref=main" -OutFile .env.playbook
```

A fetched `.env.playbook` is plain `KEY=value` lines: copy the ones you need into your app's `.env` (or your Citadel environment).

#### Clone[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/wsu-values.html#clone)

```
git clone https://git.wayne.edu/enterprise-apps/playbook.git
```

Warning

The token is your own: `read_api` for curl, `read_repository` for clone and Composer. Keep it out of the repo; for Composer it lives in `auth.json`.

Tip

Playbook is private on git.wayne.edu. If you get a 404, ask the Enterprise Applications team for read access.

### Related[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/wsu-values.html#related)

- [Platform presets](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/platform-presets.html)
- [Running off Citadel](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/running-off-citadel.html)
- [Environment variables](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html)

## HELMET[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/#helmet)

[Three members of the band Helmet, two guitarists and a drummer at a Tama kit, tinted blue against a hazy orange and gold backdrop](https://media.tenor.com/WmJKjN9NQqoAAAAM/helmet-band.gif) GIF via [Tenor](https://tenor.com/view/helmet-band-wilmas-rainbow-helmet-band-music-gif-25658120)

![php ^8.3](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/badges/php.svg) ![license MIT](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/badges/license.svg) ![psr-15: middleware](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/badges/psr15.svg) [GitHub CI](https://github.com/waynestate/helmet/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

**Put it on before you ship.** Security headers, a hardened session and an honest proxy check, snapped on before the first page is served.

HELMET is the Wayne State app stack's baseline runtime: one small framework-free PHP core that sends the security headers, hardens the session, decides whether the request really arrived over HTTPS, answers the load balancer's `/up` ping, and writes structured logs.

### Pick your path[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/#pick-your-path)

- **New here?** The [Quick start](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html) puts a raw PHP app behind the baseline in four steps.
- **Installing it now?** [Install](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html) has the requirements, the Composer line and the verify step.
- **Working with a coding agent?** [Your coding agent (ADVISOR)](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/advisor.html) gives it two read-only tools: the headers HELMET sends and why, and how long the app's PHP floor stays supported.
- **Looking for a setting or a function?** The Reference group starts with [Environment variables](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html), every `HELMET_` variable the package reads.

### Install[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/#install)

```
composer require waynestate/helmet
```

Then boot it once at the top of the front controller, before anything is echoed:

```php
use function Waynestate\Helmet\helmet_boot;

$helmet = helmet_boot([
    'preset' => 'citadel',
]);
```

`helmet_boot()` sends the headers, strips `X-Powered-By`, and answers `/up` with `200 ok` before your code runs. It returns the nonce, the logger and the request ID so the rest of the app can use them.

Version 0.4.0, MIT licensed.

Agents: the machine-readable map of these docs lives at [https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt).

Milquetoast is a Helmet song. It is not a Content-Security-Policy.

Every `HELMET_` environment variable the package reads, with its meaning, default and the file that reads it, is in [the configuration reference](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html).

---

Source: https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html

## Install[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#install)

### Requirements[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#requirements)

PHP `^8.3`. `composer.json` declares no `ext-*` extensions, so plain PHP 8.3 or newer is enough; Composer pulls the rest (Monolog, the PSR interfaces, csp-builder, the Prometheus client and symfony/http-foundation).

### Install[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#install-1)

```
composer require waynestate/helmet
```

The same line works for a raw PHP app, a Laravel app, or a PSR-15 stack: HELMET ships one package for every platform, so the adapters come with it, nothing extra to require.

Note

The example everywhere in these docs uses `'preset' => 'citadel'`, which trusts the Docker bridge gateway in front of HA-Proxy. Off the WSU platform, skip the preset and pass your own list of the addresses your front proxy connects from.

### Verify[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#verify)

Boot the package as the [Quick start](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html) does, then ask the load balancer's question:

```
curl -sI http://localhost/up
```

Expected: `200 ok`, the baseline headers on the response (`Content-Security-Policy`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN`, and the rest), and no `X-Powered-By` header. If `/up` answers before your code runs, HELMET is on the field.

### Next steps[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#next-steps)

- [Quick start](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html): the whole thing in four steps.
- Usage by stack: [Raw PHP](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-raw-php.html), [PSR-15 middleware](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-psr15.html), [Laravel](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-laravel.html).
- What goes on the wire: [The headers](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/headers.html).
- Every knob: [Environment variables](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html).

Source: https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.html

## API reference[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.html#api-reference)

Every public entry point of the `waynestate/helmet` core, with signatures exactly as they appear in the code under `src/`. For what each part does to a request, see the usage guides; for the environment variables behind the Laravel adapter, see [Environment variables](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html).

### Global functions[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.html#global-functions)

File `src/functions.php`, namespace `Waynestate\Helmet`:

| Function | Signature |
| --- | --- |
| `helmet_boot()` | `function helmet_boot(array $config): array` |
| `helmet_up_response()` | `function helmet_up_response(): array` |
| `helmet_up()` | `function helmet_up(): never` |
| `helmet_forbidden_response()` | `function helmet_forbidden_response(): array` |
| `helmet_forbidden()` | `function helmet_forbidden(): never` |
| `helmet_csp_nonce_meta()` | `function helmet_csp_nonce_meta(string $nonce): string` |
| `helmet_csp_nonce_swap()` | `function helmet_csp_nonce_swap(string $html, string $nonce, string $placeholder = 'CSP_NONCE_SLOT_FOR_HELMET'): string` |
| `helmet_metrics()` | `function helmet_metrics(array $config): array` |
| `helmet_metrics_env()` | `function helmet_metrics_env(): array` |
| `helmet_metrics_requests()` | `function helmet_metrics_requests(array $config): ?RequestMetrics` |
| `helmet_metrics_track()` | `function helmet_metrics_track(array $config): RequestTimer` |

What each one returns, from the docblocks:

- `helmet_boot()` boots the core for raw PHP: it validates the config and returns `array{nonce: string, logger: LoggerInterface|null, request_id: string}`. It throws `UnknownPresetException` for an unknown preset, `\InvalidArgumentException` for a bad config value, `InvalidCspReportUriException` for a bad report URI, and `\LogicException` if a session is already active.
- `helmet_up_response()` and `helmet_forbidden_response()` return the answer as data, `array{status: int, headers: array<string, string>, body: string}`, without sending anything; the caller sends it. `helmet_up()` and `helmet_forbidden()` send the same answers (200, body "ok", and 403, body "Forbidden") and exit, so a small public file can answer a probe that never reaches `helmet_boot()`.
- `helmet_csp_nonce_meta()` builds the `<meta property="csp-nonce">` tag that Vite's dev runtime reads to nonce the CSS and preload tags it adds after page load. Print it in `<head>` of every page, with the same nonce `helmet_boot()` returned; the nonce is escaped so a quote cannot break out of the attribute.
- `helmet_csp_nonce_swap()` replaces every occurrence of the placeholder (default `CSP_NONCE_SLOT_FOR_HELMET`, the value a built Vue/Vite page carries where Vite's `html.cspNonce` stood) with the nonce, HTML-escaped exactly like `helmet_csp_nonce_meta()` escapes it. It is pure: no output, no headers, no globals. A placeholder shorter than 16 characters throws `\InvalidArgumentException`, as does an empty nonce, and a page without the placeholder is returned unchanged.
- `helmet_metrics()` builds the `/metrics` answer as data, `array{status: int, content_type: string, body: string}`. It is fail-closed: disabled gives 404, enabled but unauthorized gives 403, and enabled but misconfigured (no token and no allow list) gives 404 plus a warning. With `storage` set, the request metrics are read back from that store and added to the body.
- `helmet_metrics_env()` reads the `HELMET_METRICS_*` variables (and `HELMET_POLICY_PATH`, as a `policy` source) the same way the Laravel config does, through `Setting::get()`, and returns them as a config array for `helmet_metrics()` and `helmet_metrics_track()`. Everything is off when nothing is set.
- `helmet_metrics_requests()` returns the `RequestMetrics` recorder when `enabled` is true and `storage` names a shared store, else null. A store that cannot be used here is logged through `logger` and treated as off.
- `helmet_metrics_track()` starts a `RequestTimer` for this request and records it once at shutdown (so a page that ends with `exit` is counted). It is inert when request metrics are off.

File `src/Ribbon/functions.php`, namespace `Waynestate\Helmet\Ribbon`:

| Function | Signature |
| --- | --- |
| `helmet_ribbon()` | `function helmet_ribbon(string $environment, bool $enabled = true, ?string $policyPath = null): Ribbon` |

A convenience helper for raw PHP apps: it creates a `Ribbon` for the given environment, which you render with its `html()` method and inject near the top of the page. When a policy path is given, the ribbon also shows a version warning for the running PHP version from CREED's policy.json; a missing, unreadable or invalid policy file produces no warning and never breaks the page.

### Advisor[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.html#advisor)

#### `Advisor\HelmetModule` [#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.html#advisor-helmetmodule)

`final class HelmetModule implements Module` in `src/Advisor/HelmetModule.php`. HELMET's [ADVISOR](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/advisor.html) module: two read-only tools, `helmet_headers` and `helmet_php_support`, that answer from HELMET's own code, in-process, about an app inside the project root. It loads only inside ADVISOR (`waynestate/advisor` is a suggestion, never a requirement) when the app's `modules.json` names it.

| Member | Signature |
| --- | --- |
| `TOOL` | `public const TOOL = 'helmet';` |
| `VERDICT` | `public const VERDICT = 'HELMET reports; PROCTOR decides.';` |
| `NONCE_PLACEHOLDER` | `public const NONCE_PLACEHOLDER = 'PerRequestNonce';` |
| `__construct()` | `public function __construct(private readonly ModuleContext $context)` |
| `id()` | `public function id(): string` |
| `tools()` | `public function tools(): array` |
| `resources()` | `public function resources(): array` |

### Csrf[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.html#csrf)

#### `Csrf\RequestForgeryGuard` [#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.html#csrf-requestforgeryguard)

`final class RequestForgeryGuard implements MiddlewareInterface` in `src/Csrf/RequestForgeryGuard.php`. PSR-15 middleware that rejects cross-site request forgery. Safe methods always pass; for every other method it reads `Sec-Fetch-Site` first (`same-origin` and `none` pass, `same-site` passes only when `allowSameSite` is true, cross-site or an unknown value is rejected), then falls back to the `Origin` header (the request's own origin and configured trusted origins pass, `Origin: null` and an unparseable origin are rejected, an absent origin passes). The rejection is 403, `text/plain`, `Cache-Control: no-store`, body "Forbidden"; it never echoes request headers.

| Member | Signature |
| --- | --- |
| `SAFE_METHODS` | `public const SAFE_METHODS = ['GET', 'HEAD', 'OPTIONS'];` |
| `__construct()` | `public function __construct(private readonly TrustedProxies $proxies, private readonly ?ResponseFactoryInterface $responseFactory = null, private readonly ?StreamFactoryInterface $streamFactory = null, private readonly bool $allowSameSite = false, array $trustedOrigins = [], array $except = [], private readonly ?LoggerInterface $logger = null)` |
| `process()` | `public function process(ServerRequestInterface $request, RequestHandlerInterface $handler): ResponseInterface` |
| `allows()` | `public function allows(string $method, string $path, ?string $secFetchSite, ?string $origin, ?string $requestOrigin): bool` |
| `originFromServerParams()` | `public static function originFromServerParams(array $serverParams, TrustedProxies $proxies): ?string` |
| `canonicalOrigin()` | `public static function canonicalOrigin(string $origin): ?string` |

### Error[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.html#error)

#### `Error\GenericErrorResponse` [#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.html#error-genericerrorresponse)

`final class GenericErrorResponse` in `src/Error/GenericErrorResponse.php`. Builds the generic error pages HELMET serves instead of a stack trace. For an uncaught exception the user gets a neutral 500 page that says nothing about what broke; the full detail goes to the log at error level, and a logger that throws never changes the answer. For a client fault the app asks for a fixed 4xx page by status code. The page text comes only from a constant map, so nothing from the request or an exception can ever reach the body.

| Member | Signature |
| --- | --- |
| `build()` | `public function build(\Throwable $e, ?LoggerInterface $logger = null): array` |
| `clientError()` | `public function clientError(int $status): array` |

### Headers[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.html#headers)

#### `Headers\SecurityHeaders` [#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.html#headers-securityheaders)

`final class SecurityHeaders` in `src/Headers/SecurityHeaders.php`. The header builders: the default CSP policy, per-request nonces, HSTS, cross-origin isolation, the permissions policy, and the full header set for one request.

#### `Headers\HeaderReasons` [#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.html#headers-headerreasons)

`final class HeaderReasons` in `src/Headers/HeaderReasons.php`. Why HELMET sends each header and each CSP directive, a sentence or two apiece, kept next to the policy it explains. The ADVISOR tool `helmet_headers` and the docs read it, and a test fails when a header or directive is added without a reason.

| Member | Signature |
| --- | --- |
| `directive()` | `public static function directive(string $directive): ?string` |
| `header()` | `public static function header(string $header): ?string` |
| `directives()` | `public static function directives(): array` |
| `headers()` | `public static function headers(): array` |

#### `Headers\SecurityHeadersMiddleware` [#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.html#headers-securityheadersmiddleware)

`final class SecurityHeadersMiddleware implements MiddlewareInterface` in `src/Headers/SecurityHeadersMiddleware.php`. PSR-15 middleware that sends HELMET's security headers. It decides whether the request is HTTPS from the trusted-proxy list, builds the headers (including a per-request CSP nonce), exposes the nonce to the application as the `helmet.csp_nonce` request attribute, and removes the `X-Powered-By` header. The headers are sent even when the inner handler throws; by default the middleware rethrows so the framework's error handler still runs, and with `rethrow` false it returns a 500 response carrying the same headers.

| Member | Signature |
| --- | --- |
| `__construct()` | `public function __construct(private readonly TrustedProxies $proxies, ?array $cspPolicy = null, private readonly bool $rethrow = true, private readonly ?ResponseFactoryInterface $responseFactory = null, private readonly int $hstsMaxAge = 31536000, private readonly bool $hstsIncludeSubDomains = true, private readonly ?string $cspReportUri = null, private readonly bool $cspReportOnly = false, private readonly ?string $coop = 'same-origin', private readonly ?string $corp = null, private readonly ?array $permissionsPolicy = null, private readonly bool $hstsPreload = false, private readonly bool $trustedTypesEnabled = false, private readonly array $trustedTypesPolicies = ['default'], private readonly bool $noStoreEnabled = false, private readonly array $noStorePaths = [])` |
| `process()` | `public function process(ServerRequestInterface $request, RequestHandlerInterface $handler): ResponseInterface` |

#### `Headers\InvalidCspReportUriException` [#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.html#headers-invalidcspreporturiexception)

`final class InvalidCspReportUriException extends InvalidArgumentException` in `src/Headers/InvalidCspReportUriException.php`. Thrown when the configured CSP report URI is not a valid report destination: it must be an absolute `https://` URL with a host, or a path relative to the page's origin that starts with a single slash. A report endpoint the browser cannot reach is worse than none, and a malformed value can break the Reporting-Endpoints header or inject a second header line.

| Member | Signature |
| --- | --- |
| `__construct()` | `public function __construct(string $uri)` |

### Health[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.html#health)

#### `Health\HealthCheck` [#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.html#health-healthcheck)

`final class HealthCheck implements MiddlewareInterface` in `src/Health/HealthCheck.php`. Answers the health check path (default `/up`) with 200 and the body "ok" without touching the application, so a running container reports up even while the app is slow. Any other request is passed through unchanged.

| Member | Signature |
| --- | --- |

### Laravel[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.html#laravel)

The Laravel adapter. The service provider wires the config into the app; the four middlewares put the core classes into the request pipeline; the two route classes register the optional endpoints, which stay off until an app opts in.

#### `Laravel\HelmetServiceProvider` [#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.html#laravel-helmetserviceprovider)

`final class HelmetServiceProvider extends ServiceProvider` in `src/Laravel/HelmetServiceProvider.php`. Merges and publishes `config/helmet.php`, copies `helmet.proxies` into Laravel's trusted-proxy list when the app has not set `trustedproxy.proxies` itself (an explicit `trustProxies(at: ...)` call still wins), and registers the `cspReport` and `helmetMetrics` route macros. It registers no routes of its own; the `/up` health route is left to Laravel's built-in `health: '/up'` option.

| Member | Signature |
| --- | --- |
| `register()` | `public function register(): void` |
| `boot()` | `public function boot(): void` |

#### `Laravel\SecurityHeaders` [#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.html#laravel-securityheaders)

`final class SecurityHeaders` in `src/Laravel/SecurityHeaders.php`. The Laravel adapter for the security headers. It reads the `helmet` config and merges per-directive CSP overrides over the core default, sends the same header set as the core middleware, resets the Vite nonce to a fresh random one after the response (a nonce that outlives its request is a nonce an attacker may have seen), and injects a `<meta property="csp-nonce">` tag right after the opening `<head>` tag in HTML responses. A nonce page differs per request, so on an HTML response whose `Cache-Control` names `public` or `s-maxage` it replaces `public` with `private` and drops `s-maxage`; every other directive, and every non-HTML response, is left exactly as written.

| Member | Signature |
| --- | --- |
| `handle()` | `public function handle(Request $request, Closure $next): Response` |

#### `Laravel\RequestForgeryGuard` [#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.html#laravel-requestforgeryguard)

`final class RequestForgeryGuard` in `src/Laravel/RequestForgeryGuard.php`. The Laravel adapter for the request-forgery guard. When it is enabled it applies the same rule the core PSR-15 middleware and `helmet_boot()` use, through the core `RequestForgeryGuard`, so every consumer path agrees; otherwise the request passes through untouched.

| Member | Signature |
| --- | --- |
| `handle()` | `public function handle(Request $request, Closure $next): Response` |

#### `Laravel\ForwardedProtoNormalizer` [#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.html#laravel-forwardedprotonormalizer)

`final class ForwardedProtoNormalizer` in `src/Laravel/ForwardedProtoNormalizer.php`. Makes Laravel agree with HELMET's HTTPS detection. When the request comes from a trusted proxy and `X-Forwarded-Proto` carries more than one value, the header is rewritten to the last value (the one the closest proxy appended) before any code reads it, because Symfony's `Request::isSecure()` reads the first value, which is the client's. Requests from untrusted peers are left alone.

| Member | Signature |
| --- | --- |
| `handle()` | `public function handle(Request $request, Closure $next): Response` |

#### `Laravel\InjectRibbon` [#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.html#laravel-injectribbon)

`final class InjectRibbon` in `src/Laravel/InjectRibbon.php`. Injects the environment ribbon into HTML responses so a developer or operator can see at a glance that they are not looking at production. It is injected only when `config('helmet.ribbon')` is true, the response `Content-Type` is HTML, and the environment is one of the non-production ones (local, development, dev, testing, test, staging); it is never injected for production, prod, live, or an empty environment. The ribbon HTML goes right after the opening `<body>` tag, and a ribbon error never breaks the page.

| Member | Signature |
| --- | --- |
| `handle()` | `public function handle(Request $request, Closure $next): Response` |

#### `Laravel\CspReportController` [#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.html#laravel-cspreportcontroller)

`final class CspReportController` in `src/Laravel/CspReportController.php`. Receives browser CSP violation reports. Reports can be numerous and can be large, so the controller caps the body size, accepts only the two report content types, and logs one line per violation (the violated directive, the blocked URI's host, and the document path), never the full body. The legacy `application/csp-report` body is a single object with the report under `csp-report` (kebab-case fields); the Reporting API `application/reports+json` body is a JSON array of report objects, and only the csp-violation entries are logged because browsers batch other report types into the same POST.

| Member | Signature |
| --- | --- |
| `MAX_BODY_BYTES` | `public const int MAX_BODY_BYTES = 16 * 1024;` |
| `MAX_REPORTS` | `public const int MAX_REPORTS = 20;` |
| `__invoke()` | `public function __invoke(Request $request): Response` |

#### `Laravel\CspReportRoute` [#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.html#laravel-cspreportroute)

`final class CspReportRoute` in `src/Laravel/CspReportRoute.php`. Registers the `Route::cspReport()` macro and the POST route it creates. The route carries no authentication of its own (an app that wants to keep the endpoint private should wrap it in its own middleware or route group), excludes the web group's CSRF middleware (browsers POST reports without a CSRF token, and the middleware would reject them with 419), and is throttled by default because the endpoint is public and its input is attacker-influenced; pass `null` as the second argument to register it without a throttle.

| --- | --- |
| `DEFAULT_PATH` | `public const string DEFAULT_PATH = '/csp-report';` |
