| `DEFAULT_THROTTLE` | `public const string DEFAULT_THROTTLE = 'throttle:60,1';` |
| `registerMacro()` | `public static function registerMacro(): void` |
| `register()` | `public static function register(string $path = self::DEFAULT_PATH, ?string $throttle = self::DEFAULT_THROTTLE): \Illuminate\Routing\Route` |

#### `Laravel\MetricsController` [#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.html#laravel-metricscontroller)

`final class MetricsController` in `src/Laravel/MetricsController.php`. Serves the metrics endpoint, fail-closed. When `helmet.metrics.enabled` is false (the default) it answers 404 so the route is not advertised; when it is enabled, a request is served only if it presents the configured bearer token or comes from an allowed client IP, anything else is 403; when it is enabled but neither a token nor an allow list is configured, it answers 404 and logs a warning, because a misconfiguration must not serve metrics. The client IP is resolved through the `helmet.proxies` trusted-proxy list, so a spoofed `X-Forwarded-For` from an untrusted peer cannot grant access.

| Member | Signature |
| --- | --- |
| `__invoke()` | `public function __invoke(Request $request): Response` |

The PHP support metrics come from a bound `PolicySource`, else from `helmet.policy_path`. The request metrics come from `RequestMetricsBinding` when `helmet.metrics.storage` is set.

#### `Laravel\RecordRequestMetrics` [#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.html#laravel-recordrequestmetrics)

`final class RecordRequestMetrics` in `src/Laravel/RecordRequestMetrics.php`. The outermost global middleware, added by the provider only when `helmet.metrics.enabled` is true and `helmet.metrics.storage` names a store. It records in `terminate()`, after the response is sent. The route group is the route name, else its URI template, else `unmatched`; the path is never a label.

The route is a plain GET to `MetricsController` and carries no authentication of its own: the controller enforces the bearer token and the client IP allow list from the `helmet.metrics` config. ### Logging[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.html#logging)

#### `Logging\Logging` [#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.html#logging-logging)

`final class Logging` in `src/Logging/Logging.php`. Creates a Monolog logger that writes JSON lines at the given minimum level, easy to ship to a log aggregator and to grep on the host. Secrets stay out of the logs: a processor redacts known sensitive keys (passwords, tokens, session IDs, keys, connection strings) from the record's context and extra before anything is written. A logging failure never takes the request down: the configured stream is wrapped in a fallback, so if it cannot be written the record goes to `php://stderr` instead. Every record also carries a request ID in `extra.request_id`, generated by HELMET and never taken from an inbound header, so the lines of one request can be tied together.

| Member | Signature |
| --- | --- |
| `create()` | `public static function create(string $channel, string $streamOrPath, string $level = 'info', ?string $requestId = null): LoggerInterface` |
| `requestId()` | `public static function requestId(): string` |
| `isValidRequestId()` | `public static function isValidRequestId(string $id): bool` |
| `addRequestId()` | `public static function addRequestId(LogRecord $record): LogRecord` |
| `redact()` | `public static function redact(LogRecord $record): LogRecord` |

### Metrics[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.html#metrics)

#### `Metrics\Metrics` [#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.html#metrics-metrics)

`final class Metrics` in `src/Metrics/Metrics.php`. Framework-free builder of the metrics payload: it knows nothing about Laravel, raw PHP, or any web framework. It builds a CollectorRegistry of request-free gauges (`helmet_info`, `wsu_stack_info` and, when a policy source is given, `helmet_php_version_status` and `helmet_php_eol_timestamp_seconds`, looked up by the running PHP's major.minor), adds the request metrics when a `RequestMetrics` is given (with `helmet_metrics_storage_up`, 0 when the store did not answer), and renders the result in the Prometheus text exposition format. The request-free gauges stay in an InMemory registry built for each scrape, so a stale label never outlives a restart.

#### `Metrics\RequestMetrics` [#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.html#metrics-requestmetrics)

`final class RequestMetrics` in `src/Metrics/RequestMetrics.php`. The opt-in request metrics on shared storage: `helmet_http_request_duration_seconds` (a histogram by `route`, `method` and `status` class; its `_count` is the request count) and `helmet_csp_violations_total` (by `directive`). Every label is bounded by HELMET: a route group must match `^[a-z0-9._/{}:-]{1,64}$` or becomes `other`, a method outside the standard verbs is `OTHER`, a status is its class (`2xx`), and a directive outside the CSP Level 3 list is `other`.

#### `Metrics\MetricsGate` [#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.html#metrics-metricsgate)

`final class MetricsGate` in `src/Metrics/MetricsGate.php`. Decides whether a request may read the metrics endpoint. The decision is fail-closed: disabled gives 404 (the route is not advertised), enabled but neither a token nor an allow list configured gives 404 plus a warning (a misconfiguration must not serve metrics), a correct bearer token or an allowed client IP gives 200, and anything else gives 403. The token is compared with `hash_equals` (constant time); the client IP is the one resolved by `ClientIp`, which already honors the trusted-proxy list. An empty token is the same as no token.

| Member | Signature |
| --- | --- |
| `__construct()` | `public function __construct(private readonly bool $enabled, ?string $token, private readonly IpAllowList $allow)` |
| `decide()` | `public function decide(?string $requestToken, string $clientIp): MetricsDecision` |

`final class MetricsDecision` in `src/Metrics/MetricsDecision.php`. The outcome of the metrics gate: one of the four states above, with its status code and reason.

### Platform[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.html#platform)

#### `Platform\Presets` [#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.html#platform-presets)

`final class Presets` in `src/Platform/Presets.php`. The platform presets: each preset names the trusted proxies for a deployment platform, so an app does not hard-code addresses that belong to the platform. `citadel` trusts the Docker bridge gateway to the HA-Proxy front (a published app port that is source-NATed to the gateway address would make a direct client look like the proxy); `docker` trusts nothing, for a plain Docker deployment with no front proxy. The headers a trusted front proxy may set are the same for every preset: `X-Forwarded-For` and `X-Forwarded-Proto`. `X-Forwarded-Host` and `X-Forwarded-Prefix` are deliberately not in the set (a platform that rewrites the host would let a client pre-seed them), and `X-Forwarded-Port` is out too, because Citadel's HA-Proxy never sends it.

| Member | Signature |
| --- | --- |
| `TRUSTED_HEADERS` | `public const TRUSTED_HEADERS = ['X-Forwarded-For', 'X-Forwarded-Proto'];` |
| `proxies()` | `public static function proxies(string $name): array` |
| `exists()` | `public static function exists(string $name): bool` |
| `names()` | `public static function names(): array` |

#### `Platform\UnknownPresetException` [#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.html#platform-unknownpresetexception)

`final class UnknownPresetException extends \InvalidArgumentException` in `src/Platform/UnknownPresetException.php`. Thrown when a config names a preset the package does not know, so a typo fails loudly at boot instead of silently trusting nothing.

### Policy[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.html#policy)

#### `Policy\PolicySource` [#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.html#policy-policysource)

| Member | Signature |

#### `Policy\JsonFilePolicySource` [#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.html#policy-jsonfilepolicysource)

`final class JsonFilePolicySource implements PolicySource` in `src/Policy/JsonFilePolicySource.php`. Reads a CREED-format policy file: a JSON object with a `schema_version` and a `components` object, each component's versions under `versions` (CREED's schema) or, in an older flat file, directly on the component. A version with no `security_until` is skipped; one with no `active_until` counts as security-only. It throws `PolicyReadException` on any problem it finds: a missing or unreadable file, invalid JSON, a schema_version it does not know, or a missing `components` object. Callers that must not throw (such as the version warning at request time) catch `PolicyReadException`.

| Member | Signature |
| --- | --- |
| `__construct()` | `public function __construct(private readonly string $path)` |
| `components()` | `public function components(): array` |

#### `Policy\PolicyReadException` [#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.html#policy-policyreadexception)

`final class PolicyReadException extends \RuntimeException` in `src/Policy/PolicyReadException.php`. Thrown by `JsonFilePolicySource` when the policy file cannot be read or parsed. It has no public members of its own.

#### `Policy\VersionStatus` [#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.html#policy-versionstatus)

`final class VersionStatus` in `src/Policy/VersionStatus.php`. Determines the support status of a component version on a given date: `active` on or before its active_until date, `security` after active_until and on or before its security_until date, `eol` after security_until, and `unknown` when the component or version is not in the policy. The date is injected, so the result is a pure function of the policy, the component, the version, and the date, which makes the boundaries testable without waiting for real support windows to close.

### Proxy[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.html#proxy)

#### `Proxy\ClientIp` [#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.html#proxy-clientip)

`final class ClientIp` in `src/Proxy/ClientIp.php`. Resolves the client IP. When the peer (`REMOTE_ADDR`) is a trusted proxy, the client IP is read from `X-Forwarded-For`: the header is a comma-separated list in which the rightmost entry is the one the closest proxy recorded, so walk from the right, skipping trusted proxies, and the first remaining entry is the client. An entry that is not a valid IP address fails closed: the peer is returned instead of continuing to an earlier entry. IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses (`::ffff:a.b.c.d`) are unmapped to `a.b.c.d` before matching, so a dual-stack proxy still matches an IPv4 trust list. When the peer is not a trusted proxy, the header is ignored entirely and `REMOTE_ADDR` is the client.

| Member | Signature |
| --- | --- |
| `resolve()` | `public static function resolve(array $serverParams, TrustedProxies $proxies, ?LoggerInterface $logger = null): string` |

#### `Proxy\HttpsDetector` [#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.html#proxy-httpsdetector)

`final class HttpsDetector` in `src/Proxy/HttpsDetector.php`. Decides whether the request arrived over HTTPS. If the SAPI reports a TLS connection, the request is HTTPS; this is the only signal trusted unconditionally. Otherwise, only a trusted proxy's `X-Forwarded-Proto: https` counts, and only the last non-empty value of the list is read (the one the closest proxy appended), trimmed and lower-cased before comparison. `X-Forwarded-Port` is deliberately never read: the front proxy sets `X-Forwarded-Proto` and the port is always 443 on the TLS edge, so the port header adds no information and only creates a spoofing surface.

| Member | Signature |
| --- | --- |
| `isHttps()` | `public static function isHttps(array $serverParams, TrustedProxies $proxies): bool` |

#### `Proxy\IpAllowList` [#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.html#proxy-ipallowlist)

`final class IpAllowList` in `src/Proxy/IpAllowList.php`. Matches a client IP address against an allow list of exact IPv4 or IPv6 addresses and CIDR ranges. Every entry is validated at construction time: an entry that is not a valid address or CIDR throws, a /0 prefix (which would allow every address of its family) is refused, and the wildcard "\*" is refused, so bad config fails loudly instead of looking like working config while allowing nothing, or the wrong thing. The matching itself is delegated to Symfony's IpUtils.

| Member | Signature |
| --- | --- |
| `__construct()` | `public function __construct(array $entries = [])` |
| `allows()` | `public function allows(string $ip): bool` |
| `isEmpty()` | `public function isEmpty(): bool` |

#### `Proxy\TrustedProxies` [#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.html#proxy-trustedproxies)

`final class TrustedProxies` in `src/Proxy/TrustedProxies.php`. Matches a client or peer IP address against the list of trusted proxies. The list may contain exact IPv4 or IPv6 addresses and CIDR ranges, with the same validation rules as `IpAllowList`: an invalid entry throws, a /0 prefix is refused, and the wildcard "\*" is refused, so bad config fails loudly at boot. The matching itself is delegated to Symfony's IpUtils.

| Member | Signature |
| --- | --- |
| `__construct()` | `public function __construct(array $proxies = [])` |
| `isTrusted()` | `public function isTrusted(string $ip): bool` |
| `unmapIpv4MappedIpv6()` | `public static function unmapIpv4MappedIpv6(string $ip): string` |
| `isEmpty()` | `public function isEmpty(): bool` |

### Ribbon[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.html#ribbon)

#### `Ribbon\Ribbon` [#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.html#ribbon-ribbon)

`final class Ribbon` in `src/Ribbon/Ribbon.php`. An environment ribbon: a small visual indicator that shows which environment an app is running in (for example "STAGING" or "DEVELOPMENT"), meant to be injected near the top of the page so a developer or operator can see at a glance that they are not looking at production. It is disabled by default in production and enabled in every other environment. The environment name is escaped to prevent XSS. When a policy file is configured, the ribbon also shows a warning line for each component version that is in its security-only phase or end of life, from CREED's policy.json; a missing, unreadable or invalid policy file produces no warning and never breaks the page.

| Member | Signature |
| --- | --- |
| `__construct()` | `public function __construct(private readonly string $environment, private readonly bool $enabled = true, ?string $policyPath = null, private readonly array $components = [], ?DateTimeInterface $now = null)` |
| `shouldShow()` | `public function shouldShow(): bool` |
| `environment()` | `public function environment(): string` |
| `html()` | `public function html(): string` |

### Session[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.html#session)

#### `Session\SessionHardening` [#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.html#session-sessionhardening)

`final class SessionHardening` in `src/Session/SessionHardening.php`. Applies hardened session settings before the session starts: the secure cookie mode (`auto` or `always`, so in always mode the cookie is only sent over TLS), `cookie_lifetime` 0 (a browser-session cookie that ends when the browser closes), `cache_limiter` nocache (so pages cannot be cached and replayed with the session attached), `cookie_path` and `cookie_domain` of `/` and empty (so the cookie is host-only), and the name `__Host-WSUSESSID` on HTTPS or `WSUSESSID` on HTTP, but only while the name is still PHP's default `PHPSESSID` (an app-chosen name is left alone, because SESAME reads whatever `session_name()` returns). `session.sid_length` is deliberately not touched: it is deprecated as of PHP 8.4 and the platform image sets it to 26.

| Member | Signature |
| --- | --- |
| `SECURE_AUTO` | `public const SECURE_AUTO = 'auto';` |
| `SECURE_ALWAYS` | `public const SECURE_ALWAYS = 'always';` |
| `apply()` | `public static function apply(bool $https, ?array $settings = null, string $secureMode = self::SECURE_AUTO): void` |

### Support[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.html#support)

#### `Support\Setting` [#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.html#support-setting)

`final class Setting` in `src/Support/Setting.php`. Resolves one HELMET setting from outside the package. The real environment wins (getenv, then `$_ENV`, then `$_SERVER`); an empty string counts as not set, so a blank value in the environment falls through to Playbook. When the environment has no value for the key, the private `waynestate/playbook` package supplies it, if it is installed. When neither has it, null comes back and the caller applies its own default. Playbook is optional by design: the package never requires it, it only looks for the class. That is how a WSU value can arrive at an app without this public repo naming a single one of them.

| Member | Signature |
| --- | --- |
| `get()` | `public static function get(string $key): ?string` |

- [Proof and tests](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html)
- [Quick start](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html)

## Configuration[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html#configuration)

Every `HELMET_` environment variable the package reads, its meaning, its default, and the file that reads it. The table below is generated from the code, so it cannot drift from what the package actually reads. To set a value, add it to your environment or `.env`; for how the platform presets choose the trusted proxies, see [Platform presets](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/platform-presets.html).

### How a value is read[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html#how-a-value-is-read)

The Laravel adapter reads every value through `Waynestate\Helmet\Support\Setting::get()`. The real environment wins (getenv, then `$_ENV`, then `$_SERVER`); an empty string counts as not set, so a blank value falls through to the next source. When the environment has no value for the key, the private `waynestate/playbook` package (Playbook) supplies it, if it is installed. When neither has it, null comes back and the default in the table applies. Playbook is optional by design: the package never requires it, it only looks for the class. That is how a WSU value can arrive at an app without this public repo naming a single one of them.

### The config keys[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html#the-config-keys)

Every value above lands in the `helmet` config repo, and every other part of the package reads it through `config()`. This lists every key, one level deep; the environment variable that fills each one is in [The variables](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html#the-variables) below. Publish the config (`php artisan vendor:publish --tag=helmet-config`) to edit a key directly instead of through the environment.

| Key | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `preset` | The platform preset name that fills `proxies` (see [Platform presets](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html#platform-presets)). Read from `HELMET_PRESET`, else from Playbook; null when no preset is named. An unknown name throws at boot, even when `HELMET_PROXIES` is set. |
| `proxies` | The trusted proxies (IPs or CIDR ranges) that may set `X-Forwarded-Proto`. Filled from `HELMET_PROXIES`; only an unset variable falls back to the `preset` list. Empty trusts nobody. |
| `scope` | Where the `SecurityHeaders` middleware runs: `global` (the default) adds it to the kernel's global middleware, `web` keeps it in the `web` group only. Set with `HELMET_SCOPE`. |
| `csp` | The Content-Security-Policy as a policy array keyed by directive, merged over the core default per directive; a directive you set replaces the default's, one you leave out keeps it, and one set to null is removed. Filled from `HELMET_CSP` when it parses as a non-empty JSON array. |
| `csp_report_uri` | The CSP report destination: an absolute https URL with a host, or a path relative to the page's origin that starts with a single slash. null sends no reporting directives. Set with `HELMET_CSP_REPORT_URI`. |
| `csp_report_only` | true sends the policy as `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only`, observing violations without blocking them. Set with `HELMET_CSP_REPORT_ONLY`. |
| `csp_trusted_types` | The Trusted Types directives, appended to the report-only header only, never the enforcing one. Off by default. |
| `csp_trusted_types.enabled` | Whether the Trusted Types directives are appended. Set with `HELMET_CSP_TRUSTED_TYPES_ENABLED`. |
| `csp_trusted_types.policies` | The Trusted Types policy names, default `["default"]`. Filled from `HELMET_CSP_TRUSTED_TYPES_POLICIES` (comma-separated). |
| `coop` | The Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy value, default `same-origin`; null sends no COOP header. Set with `HELMET_COOP`. |
| `corp` | The Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy value; null (the default) sends no CORP header. Set with `HELMET_CORP`. |
| `permissions_policy` | The Permissions-Policy feature map: each feature maps to its allowlist, and an empty allowlist denies the feature. The default is a deny list; an empty map sends no header. Filled from `HELMET_PERMISSIONS_POLICY` when it parses as JSON. |
| `hsts` | The Strict-Transport-Security max-age in seconds, sent on HTTPS responses only. Set with `HELMET_HSTS_MAX_AGE`. |
| `hsts_include_subdomains` | Whether the HSTS header carries the `includeSubDomains` directive. Set with `HELMET_HSTS_INCLUDE_SUBDOMAINS`. |
| `hsts_preload` | Whether the HSTS header carries the `preload` directive. Preload is hard to undo, so enable it only when every subdomain serves HTTPS. Set with `HELMET_HSTS_PRELOAD`. |
| `no_store` | The `Cache-Control: no-store` setting. Off by default. |
| `no_store.enabled` | Whether the `no-store` header is sent on matching responses. Set with `HELMET_NO_STORE_ENABLED`. |
| `no_store.paths` | Path prefixes that carry `no-store`; empty means every response. Filled from `HELMET_NO_STORE_PATHS` (comma-separated). |
| `session` | The session cookie settings that `helmet_boot()` applies when a raw PHP app boots through it; the Laravel adapter leaves the framework's session configuration alone. |
| `session.secure` | The session cookie Secure flag: `auto` (the default) follows the request's HTTPS detection, `always` forces it for apps whose TLS terminates in front of the app. Set with `HELMET_SESSION_SECURE`. |
| `ribbon` | Whether the environment ribbon is injected into HTML responses in non-production environments. Set with `HELMET_RIBBON`. |
| `policy_path` | The path to a CREED `policy.json` the ribbon reads for version warnings; null means no warning and no file read. Set with `HELMET_POLICY_PATH`. |
| `dev_origin` | The Vite dev server origin, used in `local` only while the dev server is running; it overrides the hot file. Set with `HELMET_DEV_ORIGIN`. |
| `warn_debug` | Whether the Laravel adapter writes the `helmet.debug_enabled_in_production` warning when the app boots with debug enabled in production. Set with `HELMET_WARN_DEBUG`. |
| `warn_broad_proxies` | Whether HELMET writes the `helmet.broad_trusted_proxy` warning at boot when the trusted-proxy list holds a broad entry (an IPv4 range shorter than `/16` or an IPv6 range shorter than `/48`). Set with `HELMET_WARN_BROAD_PROXIES` (Laravel) or the `warn_broad_proxies` option of `helmet_boot()`. |
| `metrics` | The `/metrics` endpoint, in the Prometheus text exposition format. Off by default. |
| `metrics.enabled` | Whether the endpoint is on. Set with `HELMET_METRICS_ENABLED`. |
| `metrics.token` | The bearer token a scraper must present (`Authorization: Bearer <token>`); compared with `hash_equals`. Set with `HELMET_METRICS_TOKEN`. |
| `metrics.allow` | Client IPs or CIDR ranges allowed to read the endpoint without a token. Filled from `HELMET_METRICS_ALLOW` (comma-separated). |
| `metrics.storage` | The store the request metrics share between PHP workers: `apcu`, `redis` or `sqlite`. null (the default) leaves request metrics off and the endpoint reports the request-free gauges only. Set with `HELMET_METRICS_STORAGE`. See [Metrics](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/metrics.html). |
| `metrics.redis_url` | For `redis`: `redis://[:password@]host[:port][/database]`; null means `redis://127.0.0.1:6379`. Set with `HELMET_METRICS_REDIS_URL`. |
| `metrics.sqlite_path` | For `sqlite`: the database file; null means `helmet-metrics.sqlite` in the system temp folder. Set with `HELMET_METRICS_SQLITE_PATH`. |
| `csrf` | The request-forgery guard. Off by default. |
| `csrf.enabled` | Whether the guard is on. Set with `HELMET_CSRF_ENABLED`. |
| `csrf.allow_same_site` | Whether `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-site` passes. Off by default because sibling subdomains are still same-site. Set with `HELMET_CSRF_ALLOW_SAME_SITE`. |
| `csrf.trusted_origins` | Origins that may make state-changing requests to the app. Filled from `HELMET_CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS` (comma-separated). |
| `csrf.except` | Paths that skip the guard: an exact path, a prefix ending in `*`, or `*` for every path. Filled from `HELMET_CSRF_EXCEPT` (comma-separated). |

### Platform presets[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html#platform-presets)

A preset names a platform's trusted-proxy list, so an app does not hard-code an address that belongs to the platform, not the app. The presets live in `Waynestate\Helmet\Platform\Presets`:

| Preset | Trusted proxies |
| --- | --- |
| `citadel` | the Docker bridge gateway to the HA-Proxy front (see [Running off Citadel](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/running-off-citadel.html)) |
| `docker` | none: a plain Docker network with no front proxy |

Laravel reads the preset from `HELMET_PRESET` (Playbook supplies it when the environment has none); an explicit `HELMET_PROXIES` always wins over the preset. Off the WSU platform, skip the preset and pass your own list of the addresses your front proxy connects from. An unknown preset name throws at boot, so a typo fails loudly instead of silently trusting nothing.

### The variables[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html#the-variables)

| Variable | Meaning | Default | Read in |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| HELMET_COOP | Value of the Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy header; an empty value sends no header. | same-origin | config/helmet.php |
| HELMET_CORP | Value of the Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy header; unset sends no header. | none | config/helmet.php |
| HELMET_CSP | JSON policy array merged over the default CSP per directive; empty or invalid JSON keeps the default. | the core default policy | config/helmet.php |
| HELMET_CSP_REPORT_ONLY | true sends the policy as Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only, observing violations without blocking them. | false | config/helmet.php |
| HELMET_CSP_REPORT_URI | URL browsers POST CSP violation reports to; adds report-uri and report-to to the policy plus a Reporting-Endpoints header. Must be https. | none | config/helmet.php |
| HELMET_CSP_TRUSTED_TYPES_ENABLED | true appends Trusted Types directives to the report-only CSP header. | false | config/helmet.php |
| HELMET_CSP_TRUSTED_TYPES_POLICIES | Comma-separated Trusted Types policy names; replaces the default list. | \["default"\] | config/helmet.php |
| HELMET_CSRF_ALLOW_SAME_SITE | true lets Sec-Fetch-Site: same-site pass; off by default because sibling subdomains are still same-site. | false | config/helmet.php |
| HELMET_CSRF_ENABLED | true turns on the request-forgery guard for state-changing requests. | false | config/helmet.php |
| HELMET_CSRF_EXCEPT | Comma-separated path patterns that skip the guard: an exact path, a prefix ending in \*, or \* for every path. | none | config/helmet.php |
| HELMET_CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS | Comma-separated origins allowed to make state-changing requests when the Origin fallback is used. | none | config/helmet.php |
| HELMET_DEV_ORIGIN | Vite dev server origin, used in local only while the dev server is running; must be http or https on localhost, 127.0.0.1 or \[::1\]. Overrides the hot file. | none | config/helmet.php |
| HELMET_HSTS_INCLUDE_SUBDOMAINS | false omits the HSTS includeSubDomains directive. | true | config/helmet.php |
| HELMET_HSTS_MAX_AGE | HSTS max-age in seconds, sent on HTTPS only; must not be negative. | 31536000 | config/helmet.php |
| HELMET_HSTS_PRELOAD | true appends preload to HSTS; requires a year of max-age and includeSubDomains, and is hard to undo. | false | config/helmet.php |
| HELMET_METRICS_ALLOW | Comma-separated IPs or CIDR ranges allowed to scrape /metrics without a token. | none | config/helmet.php |
| HELMET_METRICS_ENABLED | true exposes the /metrics endpoint; with neither a token nor an allow list it returns 404 and logs a warning. | false | config/helmet.php |
| HELMET_METRICS_REDIS_URL | For HELMET_METRICS_STORAGE=redis: redis://\[:password@\]host\[:port\]\[/database\]. | redis://127.0.0.1:6379 | config/helmet.php |
| HELMET_METRICS_SQLITE_PATH | For HELMET_METRICS_STORAGE=sqlite: the database file. | helmet-metrics.sqlite in the system temp folder | config/helmet.php |
| HELMET_METRICS_STORAGE | apcu, redis or sqlite turns on the request metrics (counts and latency by route group, CSP violations) and names the store every PHP worker shares; unset leaves them off. Needs HELMET_METRICS_ENABLED. | none | config/helmet.php |
| HELMET_METRICS_TOKEN | Bearer token the scraper sends as Authorization: Bearer ; compared with hash_equals. | none | config/helmet.php |
| HELMET_NO_STORE_ENABLED | true sends Cache-Control: no-store on matching responses. | false | config/helmet.php |
| HELMET_NO_STORE_PATHS | Comma-separated path prefixes that carry no-store; empty means every response. | none | config/helmet.php |
| HELMET_PERMISSIONS_POLICY | JSON feature map for the Permissions-Policy header; the default is a deny list and an empty object sends no header. | the default deny list | config/helmet.php |
| HELMET_POLICY_PATH | Path to a CREED policy.json; the ribbon then shows a version warning for the running PHP (and, in Laravel, framework) version, and /metrics reports the PHP support status and end date. A missing or invalid file never breaks the page. | none | config/helmet.php |
| HELMET_PRESET | Platform preset name (citadel or docker) that supplies the trusted proxies; read from the environment, else from Playbook. HELMET_PROXIES wins when both are set; an unknown name throws. | none | config/helmet.php |
| HELMET_PROXIES | Comma-separated IPs or CIDR ranges allowed to set X-Forwarded-Proto; wins over HELMET_PRESET and is copied to trustedproxy.proxies when the app has not set it. An explicitly empty value trusts nobody. | none | config/helmet.php |
| HELMET_RIBBON | false switches the maintenance ribbon off everywhere. | true | config/helmet.php |
| HELMET_SCOPE | global puts SecurityHeaders in the kernel's global middleware; web keeps it in the web group only. InjectRibbon always stays in web. | global | config/helmet.php |
| HELMET_SESSION_SECURE | auto sets the Secure flag only when the request is HTTPS; always forces it for apps whose TLS terminates in a proxy. Anything else throws. | auto | config/helmet.php |
| HELMET_WARN_BROAD_PROXIES | true makes HELMET log one helmet.broad_trusted_proxy warning at boot when the trusted-proxy list holds a broad entry (an IPv4 range shorter than /16 or an IPv6 range shorter than /48). | true | config/helmet.php |
| HELMET_WARN_DEBUG | true makes the Laravel adapter log one warning when the app boots with debug enabled in production. | true | config/helmet.php |

### Example .env[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html#example-env)

```
HELMET_PRESET=citadel
HELMET_CSP_REPORT_URI=https://app.apps.wayne.edu/csp-report
HELMET_METRICS_ENABLED=true
HELMET_METRICS_TOKEN=change-me
```

Warning

`HELMET_METRICS_TOKEN` is a secret. Set a different value per environment and never commit it; the scraper sends it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and the package compares it with `hash_equals`.

## Proof and tests[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#proof-and-tests)

How HELMET is proven against real Wayne State applications, and how to run its test suite on a machine with no PHP. Maintainers: how to build, test and release this project, and where its data comes from, is in [MAINTAINING.md](https://github.com/waynestate/helmet/blob/HEAD/MAINTAINING.md).

### Last run[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#last-run)

| Check | Date | Commit | Result | Duration |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `composer ci` (validate, tests, Pint, PHPStan, agent-ready, docs, audit) | 2026-11-07 | 8a79b46 | pass: 585 tests, 1537 assertions; Pint 86 files; PHPStan 36 files clean; 0 vulnerabilities | 02:40 |
| Header contract suite (`tests/Contract`) | 2026-11-07 | 8a79b46 | pass: 3 tests, 196 assertions | 00:13 |
| Test suite on PHP 8.5 (`php:8.5-cli`) | 2026-11-07 | 8a79b46 | pass: 585 tests, 1537 assertions | 00:56 |

| Test suite on PHP 8.3 (`php:8.3-cli`) | 2026-11-07 | 8a79b46 | pass: 585 tests, 1537 assertions | 01:21 |

To refresh this table, run `composer ci` and the Docker commands below on the commit you want to record, then copy the summary lines into the rows. The proof runs against real Wayne State applications are not in the table: they live on the private site behind a Wayne State employee sign-in, so they cannot run on a developer machine.

### Proof[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#proof)

Proof runs against real Wayne State applications live on a private site, [proof.apps.wayne.edu/helmet](https://proof.apps.wayne.edu/helmet/), behind a Wayne State employee sign-in.

### Tests[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#tests)

The header contract suite (`vendor/bin/phpunit tests/Contract`) runs one request through raw PHP, PSR-15, Laravel HTML and Laravel JSON and checks that the security headers agree on every path.

No PHP on the machine? Fine. Docker runs the suite.

windows

```bash
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app composer:2 composer install --no-interaction
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app php:8.5-cli vendor/bin/phpunit
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app php:8.4-cli vendor/bin/phpunit
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app php:8.3-cli vendor/bin/phpunit
```

linux

```bash
docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/app" -w /app composer:2 composer install --no-interaction
docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/app" -w /app php:8.5-cli vendor/bin/phpunit
docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/app" -w /app php:8.4-cli vendor/bin/phpunit
docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/app" -w /app php:8.3-cli vendor/bin/phpunit
```

Style and static analysis come from [Pinstripe](https://github.com/waynestate/pinstripe), the stack's coding standard: `phpstan.neon` includes `vendor/waynestate/pinstripe/phpstan/raw.neon`, and `pint.json` uses the same `per` preset Pinstripe ships.

## Troubleshooting[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#troubleshooting)

This page lists the symptoms HELMET's README, CHANGELOG and test suite justify, each with its cause, the fix and a check command. If your symptom is not here, start from [Install](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html) and verify `/up` first; the band's advice applies: short songs, no filler, every part earning its place.

### Check the baseline first[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#check-the-baseline-first)

Before anything else, ask the load balancer's question and confirm the floor is on:

linux

```bash
curl -sI http://localhost/up
```

windows

```powershell
Invoke-WebRequest http://localhost/up
```

Expected: `200 ok`, the baseline headers on the response (`Content-Security-Policy`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN`, and the rest), and no `X-Powered-By` header. If `/up` does not answer before your code runs, boot HELMET at the top of the front controller, before anything is echoed, as the [Quick start](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html) shows.

### Headers and the proxy[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#headers-and-the-proxy)

#### A request that was really HTTPS is read as plain HTTP, and no HSTS header is sent[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#a-request-that-was-really-https-is-read-as-plain-http-and-no-hsts-header-is-sent)

Cause: HELMET only honors `X-Forwarded-Proto` when the connection came from a trusted proxy. A spoofed `X-Forwarded-Proto: https` from the public internet is ignored, and no HSTS header is sent for a request that was not really secure. The usual miss is a missing or wrong trusted-proxy list: the preset name is a typo, or an explicitly empty `HELMET_PROXIES=` is set (that trusts nobody, even when a preset is set; only an unset variable falls back to the preset).

Fix: use a platform preset (for example `citadel`, which trusts the Docker bridge gateway), or list only the address the front proxy connects from, never a whole private range. A broad range such as `10.0.0.0/8` also trusts other containers on the same network, and any of them could then set `X-Forwarded-Proto`. See [HTTPS, and why the proxy list matters](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/https-and-proxies.html) and [Platform presets](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/platform-presets.html).

Check:

```
curl -sI http://localhost/up
```

Expected: `Strict-Transport-Security` present on a request that arrived over HTTPS through the proxy, and absent for a request that was not really secure.

#### Boot throws because of the preset name[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#boot-throws-because-of-the-preset-name)

Cause: an unknown `HELMET_PRESET` name throws at boot, so a typo fails loudly instead of silently trusting nothing. Since 0.2.0 it throws even when `HELMET_PROXIES` is set: a typo in the preset name fails loudly at boot instead of going silently unused. The only preset names are `citadel` and `docker`.

Fix: correct the value in the environment (or in the Playbook values if Laravel reads it from there), or skip the preset and pass your own list of the addresses your front proxy connects from.

Check:

```
composer ci
```

The suite includes `tests/Platform/PresetsTest.php`, which pins the preset names and the unknown-name failure.

#### Headers are missing on routes outside `web` or on unmatched 404s (Laravel)[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#headers-are-missing-on-routes-outside-web-or-on-unmatched-404s-laravel)

Cause: `HELMET_SCOPE=web` keeps `SecurityHeaders` in the `web` group only; then routes outside `web` and unmatched 404s do not carry its headers. By default the scope is `global`, so 404s and JSON routes carry them too.

Fix: leave `HELMET_SCOPE` at its default `global`, or set it to `global` again, if you want every response to carry the headers.

Check:

```
curl -sI http://localhost/a-page-that-does-not-exist
```

Expected: the baseline headers on the 404 response when the scope is `global`. The suite pins both scopes in `tests/Laravel/GlobalScopeTest.php` and `tests/Laravel/WebScopeTest.php`.

### The session[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#the-session)

#### Signed-in users sign in once more after deploying 0.2.1 or newer (raw PHP)[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#signed-in-users-sign-in-once-more-after-deploying-0-2-1-or-newer-raw-php)

Cause: `SessionHardening::apply()` renames the cookie while the name is still PHP's default `PHPSESSID`: it becomes `__Host-WSUSESSID` on HTTPS and `WSUSESSID` on HTTP. When an app first runs this version, existing sessions under the old name end: the next request still carries the old cookie, the app finds no session under the new name and starts a fresh one. An app that chose its own name keeps it, and SESAME reads whatever `session_name()` returns, so a changed name is safe for it. Laravel apps are unaffected (Laravel names its own cookie).

Fix: none needed; it is the expected behavior of the rename, and the `__Host-` prefix makes the browser reject the cookie unless it is `Secure`, `Path=/` and has no `Domain`. Tell app owners to expect one more sign-in after the deploy.

Check:

```
curl -sI http://localhost/up
```

Expected: the `Set-Cookie` name is `__Host-WSUSESSID` on HTTPS and `WSUSESSID` on HTTP. The values are pinned in `tests/Session/SessionHardeningTest.php`.

#### The session cookie has no `Secure` flag on Citadel[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#the-session-cookie-has-no-secure-flag-on-citadel)

Cause: by default (`auto`) the Secure flag follows the request. On Citadel, HA-Proxy ends TLS before the request reaches PHP, so the request looks plain even though the client connected over HTTPS.

Fix: set `HELMET_SESSION_SECURE=always` so the cookie keeps its `Secure` flag. In Laravel the value lands in `helmet.session.secure`; in raw PHP pass `'session' => ['secure' => 'always']` to `helmet_boot()`. Plain HTTP development keeps `auto`. The cookie name still follows the request, so it never takes the `__Host-` prefix on a plain-HTTP request.

Check:

```
curl -sI http://localhost/up
```

Expected: the session cookie carries the `Secure` flag on HTTPS responses. See [The session](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/session.html).

### The request-forgery guard[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#the-request-forgery-guard)

#### The guard answers 403 for a request that should pass[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#the-guard-answers-403-for-a-request-that-should-pass)

Cause: for state-changing requests, `Sec-Fetch-Site` is the primary signal when the browser sends it. `same-origin` and `none` pass, `same-site` passes only when `allow_same_site` is true, and `cross-site` or an unknown value is rejected. When `Sec-Fetch-Site` is absent, the `Origin` header is checked against the request's own origin and `trusted_origins`; `Origin: null` is rejected, an unparseable origin is rejected, and an absent origin passes. A rejected request receives `403`, `Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8`, `Cache-Control: no-store` and the body `Forbidden`, and the answer never echoes request headers.

Fix: pick the one that matches the caller. Set `HELMET_CSRF_ALLOW_SAME_SITE=true` to let `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-site` pass (off by default because sibling subdomains are still same-site); add the caller's origin to `HELMET_CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS`; or add a path pattern to `HELMET_CSRF_EXCEPT` (an exact path, a prefix ending in `*`, or `*` for every path).

Check: look for the warning `helmet.request_refused` in the structured log. Its context carries `event` (`request_refused`), `method` (upper case), `path` (no query string), `sec_fetch_site` and `origin_present`, which tells you exactly which rule rejected the request. The Origin value, cookies, Authorization, the `X-Forwarded-For` header, or the bad entry are never logged. The rule is pinned in `tests/Csrf/RequestForgeryGuardTest.php` and `tests/Laravel/RequestForgeryGuardTest.php`. See [The request-forgery guard](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/csrf.html).

### Content Security Policy[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#content-security-policy)

#### Inline styles vanished after overriding `style-src` with `'unsafe-inline'` [#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#inline-styles-vanished-after-overriding-style-src-with-unsafe-inline)

Cause: the policy adds the per-request nonce to `style-src` and `style-src-elem`. A browser ignores `'unsafe-inline'` once a nonce is present, so setting `style-src` to `["'unsafe-inline'"]` does not restore inline styles; it removes them.

Fix: keep the nonce, move the styles into files, or give the inline styles a nonce.

Check:

```
curl -sI http://localhost/up
```

Expected: the `Content-Security-Policy` header carries the per-request nonce in `style-src` and `style-src-elem`. See [Customizing the CSP](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/csp.html).

#### Scripts or styles are blocked in a Laravel app that uses Vite or Inertia[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#scripts-or-styles-are-blocked-in-a-laravel-app-that-uses-vite-or-inertia)

Cause: one of the rules that keep the CSP honest is being broken. The CSP has no `'unsafe-inline'` for scripts, so every `<script>` without a `src` needs `nonce="{{ Vite::cspNonce() }}"`. Inertia's `<Head>` renders into the document head after the page loads, so a `<script>` there would not carry the nonce and the browser blocks it. If another package calls `Vite::useCspNonce()` after HELMET, the `@vite` tags carry a different nonce than the CSP header, and the middleware logs a warning when it detects this. A cached page carries a stale nonce, and the browser blocks its scripts.

Fix: put scripts in your layout, where `@vite` and the nonce reach them; remove the second nonce-producing package; and do not cache HTML at a layer that shares it across requests, because the nonce changes every request. In raw PHP, print the meta tag in `<head>` with the nonce `helmet_boot()` returned:

```php
echo helmet_csp_nonce_meta($helmet['nonce']);
```

Check:

```
curl -sI http://localhost/up
```

Expected: the nonce in the `Content-Security-Policy` header matches the `helmet.csp_nonce` request attribute (in a controller, `$request->attributes->get('helmet.csp_nonce')`). The agreement between paths is pinned in `tests/Headers/SecurityHeadersTest.php` and `tests/Laravel/SecurityHeadersTest.php`.

### Logs and metrics[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#logs-and-metrics)

#### A JSON log record is missing its request ID[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#a-json-log-record-is-missing-its-request-id)

Cause: every JSON log record carries a request ID in `extra.request_id`: 16 lowercase hex characters generated by HELMET, stamped by a processor pushed before the redaction processor, so a record with a `password` context key still comes out redacted and keeps its ID. An inbound header is never trusted for the ID. If the ID is missing, the logger is not the one `helmet_boot()` configured, or the app is on a release before 0.2.2.

Fix: boot with the `log` option so `helmet_boot()` hands its own logger to the guard, and upgrade to 0.2.2 or newer. To reuse an ID you already have, set `request_id` (8 to 64 letters, digits, dots, underscores or dashes); `Logging::create()` takes it as an optional fourth argument, and anything else is ignored.

Check: send a request and read one line from the log stream. Expected shape:

```json
{"message":"login","context":{"user":"alice"},"level":200,"level_name":"INFO","channel":"app","datetime":"2026-10-29T12:00:00.000000+00:00","extra":{"request_id":"9f2c1ab04d5e6f70"}}
```

Pinned in `tests/Logging/LoggingTest.php`.

#### `/metrics` answers 404 even though `HELMET_METRICS_ENABLED=true` [#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#metrics-answers-404-even-though-helmet-metrics-enabled-true)

Cause: with neither a token nor an allow list set, the endpoint returns `404` and logs a warning, so a misconfigured app does not hand its metrics to the whole network.

Fix: choose at least one way to prove who is asking: `HELMET_METRICS_TOKEN` (a bearer token, compared with `hash_equals`) or `HELMET_METRICS_ALLOW` (comma-separated IPs or CIDR ranges allowed to scrape without a token).

Check: scrape the endpoint with the token and expect the `helmet_info` gauge with the PHP and HELMET versions. Pinned in `tests/Metrics/MetricsGateTest.php` and `tests/Metrics/BearerTokenTest.php`. See [Metrics](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/metrics.html).

#### `/metrics` answers 403 on Apache even with the right token[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#metrics-answers-403-on-apache-even-with-the-right-token)

Cause: Apache with mod_php does not copy the `Authorization` header into `$_SERVER`, so a release before this one never saw the token and denied the scrape.

Fix: upgrade. HELMET now reads the token from `HTTP_AUTHORIZATION`, then `REDIRECT_HTTP_AUTHORIZATION`, then the request headers themselves. No `.htaccess` rewrite is needed.

Check: scrape with the token and expect `200` and `helmet_info`. Pinned in `tests/Metrics/BearerTokenTest.php`.

#### The request panels are empty, or `helmet_metrics_storage_up` is 0[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#the-request-panels-are-empty-or-helmet-metrics-storage-up-is-0)

Cause: request and CSP metrics only count when `HELMET_METRICS_STORAGE` names a store (`apcu`, `redis` or `sqlite`). Unset, the endpoint serves the version and policy gauges only, on purpose. When it is set but the store cannot be used (the extension is missing, Redis is unreachable, the SQLite file is not writable), the app logs `metrics_storage_unusable` or `metrics_record_failed`, keeps serving pages, and reports `helmet_metrics_storage_up 0`.

Fix: set the store, and make sure its extension is loaded (`php -m` lists `apcu`, `redis` or `pdo_sqlite`) and, for Redis, that `HELMET_METRICS_REDIS_URL` points where the app can reach.

Check: load a page, then scrape: `helmet_http_request_duration_seconds_count` appears and `helmet_metrics_storage_up` is `1`. Pinned in `tests/Metrics/MetricsStorageTest.php` and `tests/FunctionsMetricsRequestsTest.php`. See [Pick a store](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/metrics.html#pick-a-store).

#### `helmet_php_version_status` says `unknown` [#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#helmet-php-version-status-says-unknown)

Cause: no policy is set, or the policy has no entry for the running PHP release. Status is looked up by major and minor version (`8.5`), in either the flat shape or CREED's `versions` shape.

Fix: set `HELMET_POLICY_PATH` to a CREED `policy.json` that lists the release.

Check: scrape and expect `helmet_php_version_status{status="active"} 1` (or `security`, or `eol`). Pinned in `tests/Policy/JsonFilePolicySourceTest.php`.

## Upgrading[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#upgrading)

This page walks an app from one HELMET release to the next, newest first, using only what CHANGELOG.md says. One section per released version; versions with a break get Breaking, Deprecated, Steps and How to verify. The current release is 0.4.0.

### 0.4.0 (2026-11-07)[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-4-0-2026-11-07)

No breaks: an ADVISOR module (`helmet_headers` and `helmet_php_support`, read-only), opt-in request metrics (`HELMET_METRICS_STORAGE`), PHP end-of-support and stack-info metrics, `extra.http` on web request log records, and fixes to the metrics and policy file readers. This is a pre-1.0 minor: apps that pin `^0.3` stay on 0.3.x until they move their constraint to `^0.4`. Upgrade with:

```
composer require waynestate/helmet:^0.4
```

---

### 0.3.1 (2026-11-05)[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-3-1-2026-11-05)

No breaks: a boot warning for a broad trusted-proxy list (`helmet.broad_trusted_proxy`), `helmet_csp_nonce_swap()` and `GenericErrorResponse::clientError()`, and the rest of the release is docs and deploy-layer refreshes. Upgrade with:

```
composer update waynestate/helmet
```

---

### 0.3.0 (2026-11-03)[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-3-0-2026-11-03)

#### Breaking[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#breaking)

This is a pre-1.0 minor: apps that pin `^0.2` stay on 0.2.x until they move their constraint to `^0.3`. The proxy and forwarded-header changes make some requests resolve differently, so read the Security lines first:

- An explicitly empty `HELMET_PROXIES=` now trusts nobody even when `HELMET_PRESET` is set, because only an unset variable falls back to the preset, so an app that clears the list on purpose is not silently re-opened by the platform default.
- `ClientIp` fails closed on an unparseable `X-Forwarded-For` entry (for example `203.0.113.5:443`): it returns the peer instead of walking on to an earlier, client-chosen entry, so a malformed header can no longer steer the resolved client IP.
- IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses (`::ffff:a.b.c.d`) are unmapped before matching trusted proxies, for both the peer and the forwarded entries, so a dual-stack proxy still matches its IPv4 entry instead of slipping past the trust check.
- `X-Forwarded-Proto` now follows one rule everywhere, the last non-empty value in `HttpsDetector` and the Laravel normalizer, and the normalizer decides trust with the list Laravel itself uses (`trustedproxy.proxies` when set, else `helmet.proxies`, with `*` and `**` trusting every peer as in Symfony), so HELMET and the framework can no longer disagree about which value to read or from whom to accept it.
- The CSP nonce meta tag is injected only into the real `<head>`, so a literal `<head>` inside a comment, an attribute value, or a script, style, textarea or title element no longer receives it.
- An HTML response that carries a CSP nonce has `public` changed to `private` and `s-maxage` dropped from its `Cache-Control`, so a shared cache cannot store a page whose nonce differs per request.

#### Deprecated[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#deprecated)

None listed in the changelog for this release.

#### Steps[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#steps)

1. Move the constraint in `composer.json` from `^0.2` to `^0.3`, then update:
   ```
   composer update waynestate/helmet
   ```
2. Check your environment for an explicitly empty `HELMET_PROXIES=`. If you want the preset's proxies, unset the variable entirely; if you want to trust nobody, keep it empty.
3. On Citadel, confirm the `citadel` preset's NAT assumption: `172.18.0.1` is the Docker bridge gateway, the preset is safe only when the front proxy reaches the app over that bridge, and a published app port that is source-NATed to the gateway address would make a direct client look like the proxy, so the platform must not publish the app's port.
4. If you rely on `X-Forwarded-For` values, expect the fail-closed behavior: an unparseable entry makes the resolved client IP the peer, and the warning `helmet.forwarded_for_rejected` is logged with `event` (`forwarded_for_rejected`), `reason` (`unparseable_entry`) and `peer` in the context. The Origin value, cookies, Authorization, the header and the bad entry are never logged.

#### How to verify[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#how-to-verify)

```
composer ci
```

That runs `composer validate --strict`, the test suite, Pint, PHPStan, the agent-ready check, `composer docs:check` and `composer audit`. Then ask the load balancer's question:

```
curl -sI http://localhost/up
```

Expected: `200 ok`, the baseline headers, and `Strict-Transport-Security` on a request that was really HTTPS. The suite pins the new behavior in `tests/Proxy/ClientIpTest.php`, `tests/Proxy/HttpsDetectorTest.php`, `tests/Proxy/TrustedProxiesTest.php`, `tests/Headers/SecurityHeadersTest.php` and `tests/Laravel/SecurityHeadersTest.php`.

---

### 0.2.6 (2026-11-02)[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-2-6-2026-11-02)

No breaks: HTML rewrites (CSP nonce meta, environment ribbon) keep the response's view object, so `assertInertia()` and `assertViewHas()` work in apps that use HELMET, and the rest of the release is fixes, deploy-layer refreshes and docs. Upgrade with:

```
composer update waynestate/helmet
```

---

### 0.2.5 (2026-10-29)[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-2-5-2026-10-29)

No breaks: adds the agent-ready site (prompt blocks, Markdown twins, llms.txt) from Squire's kit and `HELMET_SESSION_SECURE=always`, which keeps the session cookie Secure even when HTTPS is not detected, and moves the proof page to a private site that needs a Wayne State sign-in. Upgrade with:

```
composer update waynestate/helmet
```

---

### 0.2.4 (2026-10-29)[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-2-4-2026-10-29)

No breaks: `HELMET_PRESET` (Laravel) now also comes from the private `waynestate/playbook` package when the environment has no value; the config reads it through `Waynestate\Helmet\Support\Setting`, which checks the environment first, then Playbook, then gives up. A missing preset is still not an error, and `waynestate/playbook` is suggested, never required. Upgrade with:

```
composer update waynestate/helmet
```

---

### 0.2.3 (2026-10-29)[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-2-3-2026-10-29)

No breaks: a fix. `helmet_boot()` removed `X-Powered-By` only after it had already answered the health check path, so a GET or HEAD to `/up` (the default `health_path`) still sent the header; the removal now runs before the health answer and the request-forgery rejection, so both early exits leave the response clean. Upgrade with:

```
composer update waynestate/helmet
```

---

### 0.2.2 (2026-10-29)[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-2-2-2026-10-29)

No breaks: every JSON log record now carries a request ID in `extra.request_id`, 16 lowercase hex characters generated by HELMET (`Logging::requestId()`), stamped by a processor pushed before the redaction processor. An inbound header is never trusted for the ID. `Logging::create()` takes an optional fourth argument for a caller-supplied ID (8 to 64 letters, digits, dots, underscores or dashes; anything else is ignored), and `helmet_boot()` accepts it as `log.request_id`, which must be a string, and now also returns the ID as `request_id`. Upgrade with:

```
composer update waynestate/helmet
```

---

### 0.2.1 (2026-10-29)[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-2-1-2026-10-29)

#### Breaking[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#breaking-1)

A raw-PHP app that still used the default `PHPSESSID` cookie gets the new `WSUSESSID` name (`__Host-WSUSESSID` on HTTPS), so signed-in users sign in once more after deploying. Laravel apps are unaffected (Laravel names its own cookie). The rename happens only while the name is still the PHP default `PHPSESSID`; an app-chosen name is left alone, and SESAME reads whatever `session_name()` returns. `SessionHardening::apply()` also sets `cookie_lifetime=0` (a browser-session cookie), `cache_limiter=nocache`, `cookie_path=/`, an empty `cookie_domain` (host-only) and the cookie name.

#### Deprecated[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#deprecated-1)

None listed in the changelog for this release.

#### Steps[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#steps-1)

1. Update the package:
   ```
   composer update waynestate/helmet
   ```
2. If your app chose its own session cookie name, nothing changes for it.
3. Expect one more sign-in for raw-PHP users after the deploy; tell app owners it is expected.

#### How to verify[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#how-to-verify-1)

```
curl -sI http://localhost/up
```

Expected: the `Set-Cookie` name is `__Host-WSUSESSID` on HTTPS and `WSUSESSID` on HTTP. Pinned in `tests/Session/SessionHardeningTest.php`.

---

### 0.2.0 (2026-10-29)[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-2-0-2026-10-29)

#### Breaking[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#breaking-2)

- An unknown `HELMET_PRESET` now throws even when `HELMET_PROXIES` is set. A typo in the preset name fails loudly at boot instead of going silently unused.
- The trusted-header set in the Laravel adapter was narrowed. `X-Forwarded-Host`, `X-Forwarded-Prefix` and now `X-Forwarded-Port` are no longer trusted by default. Port is out because Citadel's HA-Proxy never sends it, so a client-sent value would pass through untouched and change the port Laravel reports and the URLs it generates. Apps that need any of them choose the set themselves with `trustProxies(at: ..., headers: ...)` or `TrustProxies::withHeaders()`.
- Laravel now agrees with HELMET on multi-value `X-Forwarded-Proto`. Citadel's HA-Proxy appends the header instead of replacing it, so a client can produce `https, http`. Symfony reads the first value of such a list (the client's), while HELMET reads the last (the one the closest proxy appended). A new middleware prepended to the global chain rewrites the header to its last value when the request comes from a trusted proxy; a single value is left alone, and requests from untrusted peers are ignored as before.
- The `<head>` match when injecting the csp-nonce meta tag was fixed: the old pattern also matched `<header>` and `<headline>` and injected the tag after the wrong element. Responses that carry a `Content-Length` header now have it refreshed to the new body length after injection, so a stale length cannot cut the page off mid-tag.

#### Deprecated[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#deprecated-2)

None listed in the changelog for this release.

#### Steps[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#steps-2)

1. Update the package:
   ```
   composer update waynestate/helmet
   ```
2. Check `HELMET_PRESET` for typos; the only names are `citadel` and `docker`.
3. If your app relied on `X-Forwarded-Host`, `X-Forwarded-Prefix` or `X-Forwarded-Port`, choose the set yourself with `trustProxies(at: ..., headers: ...)` or `TrustProxies::withHeaders()` in `bootstrap/app.php`.

#### How to verify[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#how-to-verify-2)

```
composer ci
```

Then check the headers:

```
curl -sI http://localhost/up
```

Expected: `200 ok`, the baseline headers, and the csp-nonce meta tag in the real `<head>` of an HTML response. The suite pins the adapter behavior in `tests/Laravel/SecurityHeadersTest.php` and the core in `tests/Headers/SecurityHeadersTest.php`.

---

### 0.1.0 (2026-10-27)[#](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-1-0-2026-10-27)

First tagged release. There is nothing below it to upgrade from: install with

```
composer require waynestate/helmet
```

and follow the [Quick start](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html).
